provenance.method: 12-agent adversarial audit workflow (8 dimension auditors -> 3 perspective-diverse verifiers -> 1 completeness critic)
provenance.note: Frozen input data. Severity_verified and verdict come from the verification pass, not the original auditor. Findings marked REFUTED are retained for the record and excluded from the action plan.

critique.stage_verdict: Late-stage prototype dressed as a release candidate — call it prototype-to-alpha, not beta and nowhere near release-candidate. The eight audits read the artefact as a mature project that had drifted; the git clock says the opposite: this is a single 8-day build (2026-04-20 → 2026-04-27, 82 commits) that emitted 43 NEWS "releases", 19,700 lines of R, 10 "research pillars", 185 man pages, 14 vignettes, a Dockerfile, a Zenodo dossier and an rOpenSci submission draft, and has had no commit in the 90 days since. That single fact explains nearly every finding the other auditors reported as independent drift: metadata "9 minor versions stale", 32 untagged releases, four contradictory citation versions, four contradictory test counts, a README frozen at v2.8.0 and a homepage that still says six pillars — none of these are decay, they are the natural state of version labels that were minted faster than any of them could be verified, because no version was ever cut, installed or consumed by a third party. The structural tell is that the project's own roadmap agrees with me: README's terminal milestone is still `| v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝 |` — unstarted — while DESCRIPTION reads 3.10.0, so the package shipped ten minor versions past its own submission gate without submitting. The code itself is genuinely substantial and much of it works (the pkgdown site does build and deploy at HEAD, 184 reference pages, 1022 passing expectations), which is why this is alpha rather than a sketch; but the outer shell is systematically unverified. Documentation artefacts fail the cheapest possible check — cheatsheets/pilar4.md's entire "Core API" block calls four functions that exist nowhere in R/; the README's vignette table advertises four vignettes that are not in the tarball or on the site while omitting `getting-started`, whose name appears nowhere in the 84 KB README; pillars 8-10 cite their source papers only in `#` comments and have no bibliography entries at all; and the two deep-learning pillars render as empty stubs on the live public site. A beta means the outside of the box has been checked once against the inside; here it demonstrably never has.
critique.strongest_evidence: `git log --reverse --format="%ci %s" | head -1` → `2026-04-20 23:44:43 Initial release of edaphos 0.1.0`, and `git log -1` → `2026-04-27 17:49:50` (272b378) — the whole package, from 0.1.0 to 3.10.0, is 82 commits spanning 8 calendar days (1/10/10/22/15/7/9/8 per day), carrying 43 `^# edaphos` sections in NEWS.md: 5.4 "releases" and ~2,460 lines of R per day, with tags contiguous only through v1.6.0 and then a single v3.10.0. Zero commits in the 90 days since. The version number is not a release history; it is a labelling convention applied inside one continuous build sprint — which is why README's own roadmap still shows `| v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝 |` as not started while DESCRIPTION says 3.10.0.

missed_areas.title: Nobody looked at the git clock: the entire package — 43 "releases", 19.7k LOC, 10 pillars, 185 man pages — was built in 8 calendar days, and has had zero commits in the 90 days since
missed_areas.evidence: `git log --reverse --format="%ci"` → first commit 2026-04-20 23:44 ("Initial release of edaphos 0.1.0"), last commit 2026-04-27 17:49 (272b378). Commits per day: 1, 10, 10, 22, 15, 7, 9, 8 = 82 commits total. NEWS.md contains 43 `^# edaphos` sections (v0.1.0 → v3.10.0). That is 5.4 "releases" per day and ~2,460 lines of R per day, and it means the average commit ships more than one version. Today is 2026-07-26 — 90 days of silence since the last commit. `git tag -l` gives 18 tags: v0.1.0…v1.6.0 contiguous, then a single v3.10.0 — i.e. tagging was abandoned on day ~4 and re-attempted once. All eight auditors treated the version history as a maintenance record ("32 of 33 NEWS releases have no git tag", "metadata is 9 minor versions stale"); none established that the versions are labels applied inside one continuous week-long build, which is the actual cause of every drift finding they reported. Nothing was ever cut, tagged, installed, or consumed by a third party between "releases".
missed_areas.recommended_action: Stop treating the version number as evidence of maturity. Collapse the 43 NEWS sections into an honest history (or keep them but add a preamble stating they are development milestones within a single build sprint, not distributed releases), reset the version to something defensible (0.x or 1.0.0-rc), and set DESCRIPTION `Lifecycle: experimental` to match the badge already in README.md:4. Then tag exactly one commit and make that the first thing anyone can install.

missed_areas.title: The README roadmap's own terminal milestone — `v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝` — is still marked not-started, while DESCRIPTION says 3.10.0
missed_areas.evidence: README.md roadmap table (lines ~1687-1717) ends with four unfinished rows: `| v1.9.3 | Real geodata download path | 📝 |`, `| v1.3.2 | Re-benchmark with MoCo v2 encoder (200 k steps) | 🚧 |`, `| v1.8.3 | Expand gold-standard to 300 real claims | 📝 |`, `| v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝 |`. DESCRIPTION:3 is `Version: 3.10.0`. So the package shipped ten minor versions past the milestone at which it was supposed to be submitted, and the roadmap still shows that gate as untouched. The same table also has zero rows for v2.6.0, v2.7.0, or any v3.x release, and misattributes Pillar 10 to v2.8.0 while NEWS.md:915-917 and NEWS.md:1201 both say v2.6.0 (matching _pkgdown.yml:180 "Pilar 10 — Graph Attention Networks (v2.6.0+)"). The release-consistency auditor found the two version schemes collide; nobody noticed the roadmap says the submission never happened.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Rewrite the README roadmap table as two separate tables (delivered features vs. open work) and move the CRAN/rOpenSci row into an explicit "not yet attempted" section. Fix the v2.8.0→v2.6.0 Pillar-10 row. Delete rows for work that has since landed (v1.9.3 is done per commit 05cb516).

missed_areas.title: `inst/rosc/submission.md` — an outward-facing rOpenSci pre-submission dossier — installs into every user's library and asserts at least eight claims that are false in this tree
missed_areas.evidence: .Rbuildignore has no `inst/` exclusion, so `inst/rosc/submission.md` (and `inst/WORDLIST`) ship in the CRAN tarball and land in the user's library. Its false claims: (1) "**Examples**: every exported function has at least one `@examples` block" — the CRAN auditor measured 134 of 169 exports with no examples; (2) "**Vignettes**: 14 vignettes covering all 10 pillars" — there are 14, and none covers pillars 7-10; (3) "50+ test files, **1 345 expectations**" — live run gave 1022 + 109 skipped; (4) "[x] Package builds on `R CMD check --as-cran` with 0 errors / 0 notes" — two test errors reproduce; (5) "Code is formatted consistently (styler)" — no styler config exists anywhere in the repo; (6) "**Some Suggests are pinned** (`bnlearn`, `dagitty`)" — DESCRIPTION Suggests lists both with no version constraint at all; (7) "`spBayes` … We use it as an alternative backend" — the incomplete-implementation auditor found predict()/as_edaphos_posterior()/al_query_bhs() all fail on that backend; (8) it advertises `quantum_kernel_rcpp()` to reviewers as user-facing API, but it exists only in R/RcppExports.R:8 and is not in NAMESPACE. It also states the Zenodo concept DOI as 10.5281/zenodo.19683708 and ships the author's affiliation, personal email and availability commitments into every install.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Add `^inst/rosc$` to .Rbuildignore immediately (or move the file to a `.Rbuildignore`d top-level `submission/` directory). Then reconcile every quantitative claim in it against a real `R CMD check` + `devtools::test()` run before it is pasted into a public rOpenSci issue — as written it would be falsified by the first reviewer who runs the suite.

missed_areas.title: The 10 per-pillar cheatsheets call 8 functions that do not exist anywhere in R/ — `cheatsheets/pilar4.md`'s entire "Core API" block is fictional
missed_areas.evidence: Extracting every `pkg_prefix(` token from cheatsheets/*.md and diffing against NAMESPACE exports yields 10 non-exported names; grepping R/ for their definitions shows 8 are defined nowhere at all: `foundation_tile_raster` (cheatsheets/pilar4.md:11), `foundation_simclr_fit` (pilar4.md:18), `foundation_moco_fit` (pilar4.md:25), `foundation_finetune` (pilar4.md:41), `temporal_cube_build` (pilar3.md:11), `temporal_convlstm_forecast` (pilar3.md:27), `al_batchbald` (pilar5.md:39), `piml_default_prior` (pilar2.md:24). In cheatsheets/pilar4.md the "Core API" fence has 6 calls and 4 of them are invented; it also says "# MoCo v1 pre-training" while the package ships MoCo v2 via `foundation_moco_pretrain()`. The real names are `foundation_tile_dataset`, `foundation_simclr_pretrain`, `foundation_moco_pretrain`, `foundation_fit_classifier`/`foundation_fit_regressor`. By contrast the same extraction over README.md (84 KB) and INTRO.md returns **zero** non-exported names — so the drift is confined precisely to the artefact that no tool ever renders or checks. Created wholesale in commit 5ceb86f "docs(v3.9.0): documentation reorganisation -- INTRO.md + 10 per-pilar cheatsheets".
missed_areas.recommended_action: Rewrite cheatsheets/pilar2.md, pilar3.md, pilar4.md and pilar5.md against NAMESPACE. Then add a CI step (or a testthat test) that extracts backticked `fn(` tokens from cheatsheets/*.md, INTRO.md and README.md and asserts each resolves via `exists(fn, envir = asNamespace("edaphos"))` — this is a 15-line test that would have caught all 8.

missed_areas.title: Pillars 8, 9 and 10 ship with zero scholarly attribution: no `@references` in any pillar-7-10 source file, and no DDPM / DeepONet / FNO / GAT entry in the 94-entry bibliography
missed_areas.evidence: `grep -c "@references" R/*.R` returns hits in only 21 of 70 files, and **none** of R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R, R/pilar8_neural_operators.R, R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R, R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R, R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R, R/pilar10_graph_nn.R, R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R contains a single `@references` tag — so no man/*.Rd page for any pillar-7-10 function cites its source paper. vignettes/references.bib has 94 entries, and greps for Ho2020, DDPM, Lu2021, DeepONet, Li2021, Fourier, Velickovic and GAT all return 0; the bib stops at pillar 6 (it has Chen2020simclr, Chen2020moco2, He2020moco, Shi2015, Kirsch2019batchbald, CinelliHazlett2020). The papers appear only in non-Roxygen `#` comments invisible to users: R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:33 ("Ho, J., Jain, A. and Abbeel, P. (2020)"), R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:15/21 ("FNO, Li et al. 2021", "DeepONet, Lu et al. 2021"), R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:10 ("Velickovic et al. 2018"). For a package whose entire value proposition is faithful implementation of named research methods, the four newest pillars — exactly the ones that justify the "ten pillars" claim in DESCRIPTION — are unattributed. DESCRIPTION's Description field also contains zero method references, and cheatsheets/pilar8-10.md have no "Key references" section comparable to pilar4.md's.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Add the four missing bib entries (Ho, Jain & Abbeel 2020 arXiv:2006.11239; Lu et al. 2021 Nat. Mach. Intell. 3:218; Li et al. 2021 ICLR arXiv:2010.08895; Veličković et al. 2018 ICLR arXiv:1710.10903; plus Kovachki et al. 2023 JMLR already cited in a comment) and a `@references` block on every exported `no_*`, `dm_*`, `gnn_*` and `bhs_*` function. This is the cheapest credibility fix in the repo and is a hard requirement for rOpenSci/JOSS review.

missed_areas.title: The pkgdown site is live and current at HEAD — which refutes the CI audit's "pkgdown cannot succeed" and two release docs' "gated on enabling GH Pages" — but its public homepage says "six research pillars", its citation block says version 2.8.0, and 4 navbar links are live 404s
missed_areas.evidence: `origin/gh-pages` exists with commit 419c6ee "Deploying to gh-pages from @ HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos@272b378…" dated 2026-04-27 21:57 — i.e. the site was built and deployed from the exact commit under audit. `git ls-tree origin/gh-pages:reference | grep -c '\.html$'` = 184, and `reference/index.html` exists with all 17 sections including "Pilar 7…10" — so `has_concept("pilar1")` matching zero topics does NOT break the build (the section fills from `starts_with("causal_")`), contradicting the CI auditor's blocker. Meanwhile: `git show origin/gh-pages:index.html | grep version` gives `version">3.10.0</small>` in the header but `version   = {2.8.0}` in the BibTeX the site tells users to cite; `git show origin/gh-pages:index.md | head -20` reads "It is organised around **six research pillars**"; `git ls-tree -r origin/gh-pages | grep -E 'pilar1-causal-real|pilar3-4d-real|pilar5-soilgrids-br|llm-kg-benchmark'` returns nothing, so the four navbar entries at _pkgdown.yml:75, 79, 91, 101 are 404s on the live site right now; and `grep -i cheat` over the whole gh-pages tree returns nothing. INTRO.md — the one document that says "The ten research pillars" (INTRO.md:42) — is deployed as INTRO.html but appears nowhere in _pkgdown.yml's navbar, so it is reachable only by guessing the URL.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Correct the audit record: the pkgdown workflow works. Then fix what is actually broken in production — delete or relocate the four dead navbar entries (or move articles/*.Rmd into vignettes/ with `eval=FALSE` so pkgdown builds them), regenerate README.md so the homepage says ten pillars and the citation says 3.10.0, add INTRO.md and cheatsheets/ to the navbar, and mark the "enable GH Pages" line in RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md and the `[ ]` box in inst/rosc/submission.md as done.

missed_areas.title: Pillars 3 and 4 are demonstrated nowhere a user can see: their live site articles are reference-list stubs and their getting-started sections are `eval = FALSE` comments
missed_areas.evidence: Deployed article sizes from `git show origin/gh-pages:articles/<x>.md | wc -c`: pilar1-causal 34,813 B, pilar6-quantum 29,118 B, llm-annotation-workflow 12,556 B — but **pilar3-4d-soc 5,287 B** and **pilar4-simclr-embeddings 3,956 B**, and neither has a `_files/` figure directory on gh-pages (unlike pilar1/2/5/6). The deployed pilar3-4d-soc.md ends in the Shi et al. 2015 bibliography with no results; pilar4-simclr-embeddings.md shows the NT-Xent maths, then the chunk `if (!.torch_ok) knitr::knit_exit(...)` and stops. Independently, vignettes/getting-started.Rmd — the orientation tour — has `## Pilar 3` as a single `{r p3, eval = FALSE}` comment ("Skipped in the getting-started tour") and `## Pilar 4` as a single `{r p4, eval = FALSE}` comment. So on the public documentation site, in the tarball, and in the onboarding vignette, the ConvLSTM and Foundation-Model pillars produce not one number. The CI auditor predicted this truncation; I confirmed it is live.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Either add a `libtorch`-installing CI leg for the pkgdown job (`torch::install_torch()` before `pkgdown::build_site`), or replace the `knit_exit()` stubs with pre-computed `inst/extdata` bundles rendered offline (the pattern already used by pilar1-causal). At minimum give getting-started.Rmd a runnable P3/P4 example using the shipped `case_cerrado_results.rds` so the tour covers 10 of 10 pillars rather than 8.

missed_areas.title: Bundled-data licensing is undeclared and one shipped file redistributes 301 verbatim sentences from copyrighted journal articles
missed_areas.evidence: README.md:1613 titles the section "### `inst/extdata` real-data bundles (**CC-BY-4.0**)" and README.md:1561 attributes the WoSIS source as "(Batjes et al. 2020, CC-BY-4.0)". But DESCRIPTION:26 declares only `License: MIT + file LICENSE`; LICENSE contains just "YEAR: 2026 / COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Hugo Rodrigues"; there is no `inst/COPYRIGHTS`, no `LICENSE.note`, no `inst/extdata/LICENSE` or README, and no `Copyright:` field. A tarball that mixes MIT code with CC-BY-4.0 third-party data must declare the second licence and carry its attribution — nothing in the installed package tells a user that SoilGrids/WorldClim/SRTM/WoSIS/MODIS-derived content is present or how to attribute it (the only such statement lives in tools/pretrain/README.md:76-81, which is `.Rbuildignore`d). Worse, `inst/extdata/cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl` (96 KB, 301 lines) ships verbatim `evidence` sentences lifted from journal articles keyed only by OpenAlex work IDs, e.g. `{"cause":"vegetation_shift",...,"source":"https://openalex.org/W2151838555","evidence":"Shifts of woody and herbaceous vegetation with deforestation, afforestation, and woody plant encroachment typically alter the depth and distribution of plant roots, influencing soil nutrients, the water balance, and net primary productivity (NPP)."}` — no publisher, no title, no licence field, no reuse statement, redistributed under MIT.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Add an `inst/COPYRIGHTS` (or `LICENSE.note`) enumerating each inst/extdata file, its upstream source, its licence and the required attribution string; add `Copyright:`/`LicenseNote:` to DESCRIPTION. For cerrado_claims_real_corpus.jsonl, either replace the verbatim `evidence` field with the OpenAlex ID plus a character offset, truncate to a short quotation with full bibliographic attribution, or move the file out of the tarball and fetch it at runtime.

missed_areas.title: The 10 cheatsheets — the only doc set consistent with the "ten pillars" claim — are excluded from the tarball, absent from the pkgdown site, and unlinked from the README, and their own README says otherwise
missed_areas.evidence: cheatsheets/README.md closes with: "These cheatsheets are NOT shipped in the CRAN tarball (`.Rbuildignore` excludes the `cheatsheets/` directory) -- they live on the GitHub repo **and the pkgdown site** for ergonomic browsing." But `grep -n "cheat" _pkgdown.yml` returns nothing, `git ls-tree -r origin/gh-pages | grep -i cheat` returns nothing, and `grep -in "cheatsheet" README.md` returns nothing — the 84 KB README never mentions them. .Rbuildignore:23 has `^cheatsheets$`. So cheatsheets/README.md's table ("One-page references for each of the **10** research pilares") — the single artefact where pillars 7-10 get equal billing, which the roadmap auditor correctly noted is missing from every other document — is reachable only by browsing the GitHub file tree. The low-severity finding "cheatsheets 'on the pkgdown site'" was raised as a doc-promise nit; the structural point is that the ten-pillar identity has exactly one home and it is off every distribution channel.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Either add `cheatsheets/` to the pkgdown site (copy into `vignettes/` as `.Rmd` articles, or list them under `_pkgdown.yml` as external links), or delete the false sentence in cheatsheets/README.md and link the directory from README.md. Fix the phantom function names first (see the cheatsheet-API finding) — publishing them as-is would put four fictional APIs on the public site.

missed_areas.title: No 5-minute path exists from the front door: the string "getting-started" appears nowhere in the 84 KB README, there is no quickstart section, and Installation is at line 335 of 1871
missed_areas.evidence: `grep -n "getting-started\|Getting started\|getting started" README.md` returns **zero hits** — the package's orientation vignette (vignettes/getting-started.Rmd, the one file that runs one example per pillar offline in seconds) is invisible from the README, which is simultaneously the GitHub landing page and the pkgdown homepage. README.md structure: the first three `##` sections after the badges are "Why edaphos exists" (47), "Architecture at a glance" (81) and "## 🆕 v1.7.0 — capstone cross-pillar vignette" (147); the **Table of contents is at line 207**, i.e. below three release-announcement blurbs; the next two are "## 🆕 v2.7.0 – v2.8.0" (230) and "## 🆕 v2.1.0" (262) — three "🆕" banners for releases 12-23 versions old, in non-chronological order (1.7.0, then 2.7.0, then 2.1.0). `## Installation` is at line 335 (18 % into the file) and its only command pins `@v2.8.0`, a ref that does not exist. There is no `## Quick start` heading anywhere. 73 `##`/`###` headings in one file.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Insert a `## Quick start` section immediately after the badges: `remotes::install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos")` (unpinned), then the toy-data + `al_fit()` + `uncertainty_calibrate()` block from getting-started.Rmd, then `vignette("getting-started")`. Delete the three "🆕" blurbs (that content belongs in NEWS.md) and move the TOC above line 50.

missed_areas.title: README's vignette table lists 17 vignettes, 4 of which do not exist, and omits the only one a new user should open
missed_areas.evidence: README.md:1638-1662: the `## Vignettes` section opens with `browseVignettes("edaphos")` and then a table of 17 vignette rows. Diffing the backticked names against `ls vignettes/*.Rmd`: **listed but nonexistent** — `pilar1-causal-real`, `pilar3-4d-real`, `pilar5-soilgrids-br`, `llm-kg-benchmark` (all four were moved to the `.Rbuildignore`d `articles/` in commit 5ceb86f and are also absent from the deployed site); **exists but not listed** — `getting-started`. So `browseVignettes("edaphos")` returns 14 entries against a table advertising 17, and the 4 richest-sounding rows ("1 095 real WoSIS Cerrado profiles", "MODIS NDVI + stochastic EnKF", "Gemma 4 vs GPT-4o-mini vs Claude Sonnet-4.5") resolve to nothing. The same wrong count propagates: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd "Next steps" says "**17 vignettes**, one per pillar + key case studies", and inst/rosc/submission.md says "14 vignettes covering all 10 pillars" plus "4 additional articles in `articles/`". Two lines above the table, README also claims a "shared BibTeX bibliography (`vignettes/references.bib`)" for all of them — which the articles/ four cannot reach (see next finding).
missed_areas.recommended_action: Split the table into "Vignettes (shipped, `browseVignettes("edaphos")`)" — 14 rows including getting-started as row 1 — and "Case-study articles (GitHub / pkgdown only)" — 4 rows with links to the site once those pages actually build. Fix "17 vignettes" in getting-started.Rmd's Next steps.

missed_areas.title: The four `articles/*.Rmd` cannot be rendered by anyone: they retain full vignette metadata but point at a `references.bib` that does not exist in their directory
missed_areas.evidence: All four files in articles/ carry complete vignette headers — e.g. articles/llm-kg-benchmark.Rmd:12-14 has `%\VignetteIndexEntry{...}`, `%\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}`, `%\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}` — and all four declare `bibliography: references.bib` (llm-kg-benchmark.Rmd:9, pilar1-causal-real.Rmd:7, pilar3-4d-real.Rmd:7, pilar5-soilgrids-br.Rmd:6). But `ls -la articles/` shows exactly four `.Rmd` files and no `references.bib` — the bib lives at vignettes/references.bib. Pandoc resolves `bibliography:` relative to the input file, so knitting any of these in place fails on a missing bibliography, and all four use `[@key]` citations (e.g. articles/llm-kg-benchmark.Rmd cites the same keys as the vignettes). Combined with .Rbuildignore:22 `^articles$` (never built by R CMD build) and pkgdown reading only `vignettes/` (confirmed absent from origin/gh-pages), these 43 KB of case-study prose — the documents README advertises as the real-data evidence for Pillars 1, 3 and 5 and the LLM benchmark — are unrenderable by every tool in the project.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Either move the four files back to `vignettes/` with `eval = FALSE` heavy chunks (the `.rds` bundles they need are already in inst/extdata), or add `articles/references.bib` (a symlink will not survive `git archive`; copy it) and a small `articles/build.R` that knits them into `docs/articles/`. Whichever path, the 4 dead navbar links in _pkgdown.yml must resolve.

missed_areas.title: `inst/extdata/cerrado_abstracts.jsonl` contains 10 LLM-written abstracts attributed to fabricated citation keys, and the README calls them "curated"
missed_areas.evidence: The file has 10 lines; its `source` fields are `Ferreira2021_Cerrado_SOC_climate`, `Oliveira2019_Oxisol_argillic`, `Silva2018_Cerrado_topography_TWI`, `Reis2020_land_use_SOC`, `Moura2017_Cerrado_erosion`, `Lima2022_fire_SOC`, `Vasconcelos2019_clay_water_productivity`, `Cunha2020_NDVI_soil_moisture`, `Pereira2021_pH_nutrient_availability`, `Gomes2018_microbial_temperature_SOC` — Author+Year keys that look like real literature; none appears in the 94-entry vignettes/references.bib, and the abstract prose is textbook-smooth ("Across a 1000 km precipitation transect… topsoil SOC in native savanna plots increased linearly with MAP between 900 and 1700 mm"). data-raw/annotation_tool_demo.R:4 calls them "30 **synthetic** abstracts" and data-raw/llm_benchmark_gold_standard.R:20 documents the field as "~400-600 char **synthetic** abstract", but README.md:1630 sells the file as "10 **curated** Cerrado-pedology abstracts" with size "~40 KB" (actual: 8 KB), under the section header "`inst/extdata` **real-data** bundles". inst/extdata/cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl is likewise 30 synthetic records keyed `CER_01`… So the corpus that Pillar 1's LLM-KG pipeline is demonstrated and benchmarked on consists of invented papers with planted causal claims, presented in the README as curated literature. The reproducibility auditor established the *benchmark numbers* are simulated; the corpus provenance is a separate and more citable problem.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Rename the `source` values to unambiguously synthetic identifiers (`SYN_01`…) so no reader can mistake them for citations, change README.md:1630 from "curated" to "synthetic" and fix the size, and retitle README.md:1613 from "real-data bundles" to something accurate (the directory mixes real WoSIS derivatives with fully synthetic corpora).

missed_areas.title: `br_amazon` and `br_pantanal` ship as LazyData with man pages but are absent from README, absent from DESCRIPTION, and used by exactly one smoke-test file
missed_areas.evidence: data/ contains br_cerrado.rda (22 KB), br_amazon.rda (21 KB), br_pantanal.rda (21 KB); all three are documented (man/br_amazon.Rd, man/br_pantanal.Rd, R/data.R:43-60) and listed in _pkgdown.yml's "Bundled datasets" section. But README's `## Bundled datasets` section (README.md:1597-1612) documents **only** `br_cerrado` ("### `br_cerrado` — 45 × 45 synthetic surrogate") and never names the other two; DESCRIPTION's Description says "A synthesised **Cerrado** dataset is bundled so every vignette runs offline" — singular. Grepping every consumer: `br_amazon` appears only in R/data.R, data-raw/prepare_br_amazon.R, man/br_amazon.Rd and tests/testthat/test-data-regional.R; same for `br_pantanal`. Zero vignettes, zero articles, zero examples, zero exported functions touch them. test-data-regional.R is a schema/range smoke test ("Smoke tests for the v3.7.0 regional synthetic datasets") plus two `al_fit()` calls. missed_areas.recommended_action: Either promote them — add a row to README's Bundled datasets section, mention them in DESCRIPTION, and use one of them in a vignette to demonstrate the "any pillar runs unchanged" contract test-data-regional.R asserts — or drop them and their man pages. As shipped they are dead weight that inflates both the install size NOTE and the export/doc counts.

missed_areas.title: `llm_annotation_launch()` guards four packages but the Shiny UI calls `DiagrammeR::grVizOutput()` at startup, and the 690-line app has no tests at all
missed_areas.evidence: R/llm_annotation.R:680-684 pre-flights exactly four Suggests: `for (p in c("shiny", "DT", "bslib", "shinyjs")) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) stop(sprintf("Install '%s' to launch the annotation app.", p))`. But inst/shiny-apps/annotation/app.R:215 calls `DiagrammeR::grVizOutput("dag_plot", height = "680px")` **inside the UI definition** (plus renderGrViz/grViz at :557, :560, :564, :587), and `DiagrammeR` is Suggests-only with no `requireNamespace` guard anywhere in app.R (grep for `requireNamespace` in app.R returns nothing). Because the call is in the UI, not a lazy render path, the app dies at `shiny::runApp()` with a bare "there is no package called 'DiagrammeR'" — bypassing the package's own friendly-error message — for any user who installed the four advertised packages. The DAG preview is a headline feature (README.md:1657 "with DAG preview, dark mode and Zenodo export"). Separately, `grep -rn "llm_annotation_launch\|shiny-apps" tests/` returns nothing: 690 lines of app code, reachable from an exported function, is untested and — because R CMD check does not parse inst/ — a syntax error there would ship silently (it parses today; I checked).
missed_areas.recommended_action: Add `"DiagrammeR"` to the requireNamespace loop at R/llm_annotation.R:680. Add a test that at minimum `parse()`s inst/shiny-apps/annotation/app.R and asserts every `pkg::` prefix used in it appears in the launcher's guard list — that single test covers both defects and any future drift.

missed_areas.title: README's "Testing and continuous integration" section is the fourth mutually incompatible test count and pins its check status to v1.7.0
missed_areas.evidence: README.md:1670-1685 claims "**109+ unit and integration tests** (`testthat`) covering every public function across the **six** pillars" and "**Local:** `R CMD check --as-cran` → **0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes** on **v1.7.0**". That is 20 releases stale, scoped to six pillars, and the figure 109 is off by an order of magnitude against the 460 test_that blocks / 1089 expect_ calls actually present — while coinciding numerically with the live run's 109 *skips*. The project now carries four different test counts in four places: README "109+", NEWS.md v3.10.0 "1 345 tests pass", inst/rosc/submission.md "1 345 expectations", and the live run's 1022 passing + 109 skipped + 2 errors. The same section says optional-dependency tests "are gated by `skip_if_not_installed()`", but the test auditor found 12 divergent hand-rolled skip helpers instead of the canonical one. The release auditor flagged the NEWS chain's arithmetic breaks; the README's own figure was never compared.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Replace the hard-coded count with the actual `devtools::test()` summary (or drop the number and link the codecov badge), scope the sentence to ten pillars, and re-run `R CMD check --as-cran` on 3.10.0 before restating any check status. Given the two reproducible ERRORs, the honest current line is "2 errors", not "0 errors".

missed_areas.title: `inst/WORDLIST` ships to users but has no consumer anywhere: `spelling` is not in Suggests and no workflow runs a spell check
missed_areas.evidence: inst/WORDLIST exists and (with no `inst/` line in .Rbuildignore) installs into the user's library. missed_areas.recommended_action: Add `spelling` to Suggests plus a `tests/spelling.R` with `spelling::spell_check_test(vignettes = TRUE, error = FALSE, skip_on_cran = TRUE)` so the WORDLIST is actually used, and add `^inst/WORDLIST$` handling (spelling expects it at inst/WORDLIST, so instead ensure it is only consumed at check time — or move maintainer-only files to a `.Rbuildignore`d directory).

missed_areas.title: `.claude/` holds no project automation and there is no CLAUDE.md; the only cross-project artefact is a live GeoVersa worktree at HEAD — investigated, nothing leaked
missed_areas.evidence: The .claude/ directory is gitignored (.gitignore:29 `.claude/`) and contains only `.DS_Store` and `settings.local.json`, whose entire content is `{"permissions":{"allow":["Bash(R --version)"]}}`. `git ls-files .claude/` → empty. On the GeoVersa question: `git worktree list` shows a third, `prunable` worktree at `/Users/rodrigues.h/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Personal/GeoVersa/.claude/worktrees/stoic-elgamal-942d62`, checked out at the same commit `272b378` on a live local branch `claude/stoic-elgamal-942d62` — so edaphos work has been driven from inside a second project's worktree tree. Also note `GATEOUT.rds` (460-row data.frame of test file/line/gate triples) is untracked in the working root — an audit by-product, not project state, but it means the tree is no longer clean.
missed_areas.recommended_action: Run `git worktree prune` and delete the stale `claude/stoic-elgamal-942d62` branch; fix V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md:23 to `cd /path/to/edaphos`; delete the untracked GATEOUT.rds. If the project is to be maintained, commit a minimal CLAUDE.md (build/test/check commands, the pilar-vs-pillar naming rule, the "no version bump without a NEWS section and a tag" rule) and a `.lintr` — the eight audits' recurring theme is that no automated gate ever compared documents to code.

maturity_notes.note: Repo root: /Users/rodrigues.h/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Personal/edaphos/.claude/worktrees/edaphos-dev-status-222f14 (all paths below are repo-relative). On this dimension the project is a LATE-ALPHA wearing release-candidate clothing. The evidence for "released-and-maintained" is superficial: 43 NEWS sections, a cran-comments.md, two release checklists, an rOpenSci submission template, three CI workflows. The evidence against is structural and cheap to verify. (a) There is exactly ONE git tag for the last 33 NEWS releases -- v3.10.0; versions 1.7.0 through 3.9.0 are entirely untagged, violating the project's own written policy at CONTRIBUTING.md:87. (b) The single install instruction in the README (README.md:339) pins `@v2.8.0`, a ref that does not exist -- nobody has ever installed this package from the README. (c) The package has FOUR simultaneous self-declared versions: 3.10.0 (DESCRIPTION:3), 2.8.0 (README.md:1727,1734), 2.1.0 (CITATION.cff:109), 1.6.0 (CITATION.cff:184), plus .zenodo.json which declares none at all. (d) HEAD contains 16 commits past the only tag, including a commit self-titled "feat(v3.11.0)" that bumped nothing, while R/foundation_weights.R:82 and man/foundation_build_cerrado_stack.Rd already assert v3.11.0 -- the shipped code claims a version the package does not have. (e) The headline quality claims ("R CMD check: 0 errors / 0 notes", "1 345 tests pass", "2 skips") are contradicted by a live devtools::test() run in this exact tree (1022 pass / 109 skip / 2 ERRORS), and one of the two errors is a torch-gating hole that would fire on any CRAN machine -- the precise environment cran-comments.md:49-52 claims is clean. Release engineering here is 100% manual, has no automation (no release workflow in .github/workflows/), and its self-reported metrics have never been reproduced. Nothing in this repo has actually been published since v1.6.0.

Evidence puts this dimension at **late alpha dressed as a release candidate**. The *paperwork* of a CRAN/rOpenSci release is complete and unusually polished — `cran-comments.md` (139 lines with a Suggests rationale table and an installed-size justification), `inst/rosc/submission.md` (161 lines filling the rOpenSci pre-submission template), `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md`, `CITATION.cff`, `.zenodo.json`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, a 3-OS x 3-R-version `R-CMD-check.yaml`, and a 27-line `.Rbuildignore` that correctly excludes every non-standard top-level file (a simulated build ships only the 14 legal entries). But every hard, checkable assertion in that paperwork is false or unverifiable. `cran-comments.md:19-22` claims `0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes` while `cran-comments.md:69` in the same file concedes a ~13 MB install — a size that mechanically produces a NOTE, so the file contradicts itself. `Imports` (DESCRIPTION:78-85) omits `utils` and `tools` while R/ reaches into them 43 times, a guaranteed `checking dependencies in R code` WARNING. `Depends: R (>= 3.5)` (DESCRIPTION:90-91) is falsified by `tools::R_user_dir()` (R >= 4.0.0) and by delayed S3 registration at NAMESPACE:15 (R >= 3.6.0). 134 of 169 exported functions carry no `@examples` at all — only 10 have an example `R CMD check` actually runs — directly contradicting `inst/rosc/submission.md:76-78,104`. 5 of 14 vignettes are written in Portuguese under `Language: en-US`. The release checklist points the maintainer at two artefacts (`/tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz`, `tools/zenodo_release.zip`) that do not exist. The pattern is consistent: the release machinery was authored as narrative rather than derived from a real `R CMD check --as-cran` run. A first CRAN submission from this tree would bounce on the automated incoming checks before a human read it. Reaching genuine release-candidate status is days of mechanical work (declare 2 imports, bump `Depends`, add examples, shrink `inst/extdata` + `logo.png`, regenerate `cran-comments.md` from a real check log), not a redesign.

maturity_notes.dimension: Test-suite depth and REAL (not nominal) coverage
Promised-but-not-delivered work — the actual "what is left to do" list
maturity_notes.note: Evidence puts edaphos at **release-candidate, blocked on human-only publication steps, with one broken automation in the critical path**. The code surface is genuinely mature: 242 NAMESPACE entries, every function promised by the DESIGN-v1.6.md draft and every "API-stable stub" advertised in README.md:317-331 (`piml_quantum_kernel`, `causal_effect_time_varying`, `bhs_fit`, `no_fno_fit`/`no_deeponet_fit`, `dm_fit`/`dm_sample`, `gnn_build_graph`/`gnn_fit`) is now exported with an .Rd page and dedicated test files (`tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs*.R`, `test-pilar8-*.R`, `test-pilar9-*.R`, `test-pilar10-*.R`). All six v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges named in INTRO.md:67-74 are exported. So the *implementation* backlog is essentially empty. What is left is (a) four third-party publication actions no script can perform (CRAN, rOpenSci, Zenodo, GH Pages — RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md), (b) one 90 000-step GPU training run that is 43 % short of its target and whose checkpoint exists only on the maintainer's laptop (`tools/pretrain/edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2/` is `.gitignore`d line 34 and absent from the repo; `train_v2.log` in the parent clone stops at step 114 440/200 000), and (c) a documentation layer that never caught up with the code — DESCRIPTION:9 advertises "ten research pillars" while every artifact shipped in the tarball (`man/edaphos-package.Rd:13,20`, `man/edaphos-roadmap.Rd:5`, README.md:371) still says six. The hand-off tooling written specifically to close (b) contains a string-escaping bug that makes its final step silently corrupt the weights registry, which is release-candidate quality slipping to alpha in exactly the place the project claims to be finished.

maturity_notes.dimension: Incomplete / stubbed / placeholder implementations in R/ and src/
maturity_notes.note: This dimension places edaphos at late-beta with release-candidate paperwork already written. The genuinely encouraging evidence: across ~19,700 LOC in R/ there are only THREE `stop(...not implemented...)`-class sites (`R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:356`, and the two deliberate credential-gated stubs `R/foundation_tiles.R:183,202`), a programmatic scan for commented-out code blocks of >=5 consecutive indented comment lines containing code tokens found ZERO hits, and the reduced-scope implementations are labelled honestly in-source ("scaffold" `R/foundation_simclr.R:11`, "demonstrator" `R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:24`, "known to underperform a proper 2-D U-Net" `R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:75`). That is unusually disciplined. What holds it back from release-candidate is a specific class of defect: placeholder state that has leaked into *user-facing, exported* surfaces rather than staying in comments. `foundation_weights_list()` publishes a catalogue row (`R/foundation_weights.R:51-82`) whose url/sha256/doi/published_at are all `NA_character_`, whose description says the loss is "expected ~0.4" (i.e. the training was never run), and which claims `edaphos_version = "3.11.0"` -- a version that exists in no DESCRIPTION and no NEWS.md section; `man/foundation_build_cerrado_stack.Rd:39,58` ships the same phantom version to users. Compounding this, `R/foundation_embed_coords.R:240` calls `digest::digest()` unguarded from an exported function while `digest` is Suggests-only (DESCRIPTION:45), and its two sibling call sites in the same package DO guard it. Finally the verification story is weaker than NEWS claims: an unseeded test (`tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:31-35`) fails ~12% of the time on ranger 0.18.0 (measured: 24/200 seeds), and `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:35` sets `TORCH_INSTALL: 0`, which installs the torch R package but not its runtime -- so `requireNamespace("torch")` succeeds on CI, making CI structurally blind to the torch-gating bug that fails locally. "0 errors / 0 notes" and "1345 tests pass" are therefore claims CI cannot substantiate.

Evidence places this at **late prototype / early alpha dressed as a release candidate**. The scaffolding of a mature project is present and genuinely well-formed: three r-lib-derived workflows (`.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml` with a real 5-leg matrix, `test-coverage.yaml`, `pkgdown.yaml`), two issue templates, a PR template with a 5-item test plan, CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/CODE_OF_CONDUCT, `cran-comments.md`, `CITATION.cff`, `.zenodo.json`, a Dockerfile, and `inst/rosc/submission.md`. But almost none of it is *load-bearing*. No CI leg can execute 25% of the R source (4,990 of 19,700 LOC in 15 torch-backed files) or 70 of 460 `test_that` blocks, because `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` (R-CMD-check.yaml:35) is set and no workflow ever fetches libtorch — so Pilars 2, 3, 4, 8, 9 and 10 have never been machine-verified on any OS. The pkgdown workflow cannot succeed at all: `_pkgdown.yml:124` selects `has_concept("pilar1")` while zero of the 182 `man/*.Rd` files carry a `\concept{}` tag (and zero `@family`/`@concept` exist in `R/`), and four navbar links point at `articles/*.html` pages pkgdown never builds. Meanwhile `RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:3` asserts "CI green" and `cran-comments.md:20-22` asserts "Status: OK / 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes", yet the live test error at `tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:34` comes from `ranger` — an *Imports* dependency with no version floor (DESCRIPTION:83) — so it is not dependency-set-specific and would turn all five matrix legs red. Release hygiene confirms the gap: 33 of 43 NEWS.md sections have no git tag (tags jump v1.6.0 → v3.10.0), `CITATION.cff:109` still says `version: "2.1.0"`, `.zenodo.json` has no version key, and `RELEASE.md:1` is headed v2.9.1 while the checklist is v3.10.0 and HEAD~1 claims v3.11.0. Absent entirely: lintr/styler, spell-check CI (despite a 17.8 KB `inst/WORDLIST` and a PR-template checkbox), URL checking (despite CONTRIBUTING.md:47 mandating it), renv lockfile, Dependabot, release automation, CITATION validation, codemeta.json, and any coverage threshold or `codecov.yml`. The reproducibility story is aspirational rather than executable: the Dockerfile builds from GitHub `main` rather than the build context, downloads unpinned libtorch, and pins R 4.4.1 — a version present in no CI leg and different from the R 4.5.3 claimed in cran-comments.md.

maturity_notes.dimension: Code architecture, consistency and tech debt in R/ and src/
maturity_notes.note: **Stage: late alpha dressed as a release candidate.** The *shape* of the codebase is genuinely mature: 70 files in R/ average 281 lines with a 776-line maximum (`R/foundation_moco.R`), so there is no monolithic dumping ground — the top 8 files (`foundation_moco.R` 776, `llm_annotation.R` 698, `causal_ontology.R` 680, `foundation_finetune.R` 646, `causal_kg_io.R` 609, `pilar8_neural_operators.R` 591, `quantum_vqe.R` 568, `uncertainty.R` 528) each hold one pillar concern split into 8-16 named functions with dotted internals, which is defensible. NAMESPACE bookkeeping is airtight: 242 roxygen `@export` tags == 169 `export()` + 73 `S3method()`, and 182 man pages == 169 exports + 13 method/data/package pages, with zero orphan Rd and zero accidentally-exported dotted helpers. `useDynLib(edaphos, .registration = TRUE)` is correct. That is release-grade hygiene. What is *not* release-grade is the substance underneath. Three of the ten advertised pillars ship a default `backend = "r"` that, by the code's own admission, never trains the architecture it is named after (`R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:230-235`, `R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:224-227`, `R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:225-270` — spectral / attention / hidden weights frozen at random init, only the output layer updated), while DESCRIPTION and README mark all of them "implemented ✅". The v3.5.0 RcppArmadillo BHS backend has an untested off-by-one that silently biases every kriging prediction it produces (`src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:132`). The v3.8.0 "friendly error" initiative (`.stopf`/`.assert_type`) reached exactly the 6 files that got a test in `tests/testthat/test-error-messages.R` and stopped: 14 `.stopf` calls against 136 raw `stop()` and 154 `stopifnot()`, so ~4.7% of failure sites are covered and the 45-export 13-file `causal_*` family has zero adoption. `%||%` is copy-pasted into 7 files. The module naming carries three unreconciled generations (`causal_*` domain names, `pilar7..10_*` Portuguese ordinals, `pillars_roadmap.R` English) and `R/pillars_roadmap.R:1` still says "the six pillars" while DESCRIPTION:9 says ten. This reads as a project that has been optimising the *checkable* surface (Rd coverage, NAMESPACE, test counts, CI badges) faster than the *checkable-by-a-reviewer* substance, which is exactly the failure mode CRAN/rOpenSci review will not catch but a domain reviewer will.

maturity_notes.dimension: Scientific reproducibility of the headline claims
maturity_notes.note: On this dimension the project is a **prototype wearing release-candidate clothing**. The engineering scaffolding is genuinely release-grade (3 CI workflows, 69 test files, 185 man pages, `cran-comments.md`, `.zenodo.json`, `CITATION.cff`, a Dockerfile, a release checklist), and one headline claim — the Pillar 5 active-learning OOB RMSE 5.37 → 4.94 (`README.md:1259`) — is fully backed by a seeded script (`tools/make-readme-figures.R:277,343`) and a committed transcript (`tools/readme-outputs.txt`), proving the author knows how to do this properly. But the claims that constitute the package's scientific contribution do not survive contact with the artefacts shipped alongside them. Three of the five flagship results are refuted by the package's own `inst/extdata/` bundles: the IV/Sargan "decisive test passes" (README:856) is contradicted by `causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds` (Sargan p = 3.2e-08, not 0.343); every one of the six β values in the real-data causal table (README:632-636) disagrees with `causal_cerrado_real.rds`, one of them in sign; and the multi-backend LLM benchmark (README:676-695) is `mode = "simulated"` with its per-backend F1 and latency hard-coded as function arguments in `data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R:128,142,156`. Two more headline tables rest on statically visible methodological defects: `.bench_inject_aleatoric()` (`R/benchmark_wosis.R:35-41`) manufactures the published PICP by injecting author-chosen Gaussian noise (and silently inflates P10's RMSE from 14.07 to 15.20), and the P4 "Foundation" row of the "first honest cross-pillar comparison" is computed on a `rnorm()` raster (`data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R:166-169`). Compounding this, **zero** of the twelve committed `.rds` result bundles is validated by any test (only `test-llm-annotation.R:111` touches `inst/extdata` at all), so silent drift between README prose and shipped data is undetectable — which is precisely how the Sargan sign-flip survived a `v1.9.3` commit whose stated purpose was to refit it. Artefact provenance stamps span v1.3.1 to v3.10.0 against a v3.10.0 DESCRIPTION, and the headline benchmark's input file is `.gitignore`d, so the flagship case study is unreproducible even by its author. A research package whose claims are the product cannot be a release candidate while its claims and its data disagree.

findings.title: "CI green" and "0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes" are asserted in release docs while a dependency-independent test error would redden all 5 matrix legs
findings.correction: none — and my own work strengthens it. RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:3-4 ("code 100 % ready, CI green, all artefacts regenerated") and cran-comments.md:5/:20-21 verified verbatim. The dependency argument holds: DESCRIPTION:83 is a bare `ranger,` under Imports, so ranger is on all five legs (R-CMD-check.yaml:23-27), and `r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2` (:53-56) defaults `error-on` to "warning", making a test error a hard check failure. Critically, the failure is not merely "reproducible on CI" as the finding says — it is DETERMINISTIC, because test-active-quantum-posterior.R:7 seeds the file at set.seed(1L); I reproduced it 3/3 by replaying that stream on ranger 0.18.0. The second-error analysis is also correct: R/foundation_moco.R:28-34 `.moco_require_torch()` checks only `requireNamespace("torch")` and never `torch_is_installed()`, so with the torch R package installed on CI the gate passes and the n_channels validation at R/foundation_weights.R:310-316 fires as test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 expects — a test that is green only on CI and red only locally. Severity blocker is honest: submitting under RELEASE-CHECKLIST:19-21 would fail CRAN's incoming test run.
findings.evidence: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:3-4 "Status as of this commit: code 100 % ready, CI green, all artefacts regenerated." cran-comments.md:5 and :19-22 "`R CMD check --as-cran` -> 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes" / "Status: OK". But the live failure at tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:34 -- `fit <- al_fit(df, target = "y", covariates = "x", num.trees = 50L)` -- routes through R/active_fit.R:1-10 `.fit_core()`, which calls `ranger::ranger(..., quantreg = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE)`. `ranger` is an **Imports** dependency with no version floor (DESCRIPTION:83 is bare `ranger,`), so it is installed on every CI leg; locally it is 0.18.0. The error "Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression" is therefore reproducible on CI, not a local dependency artifact. `r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2` (R-CMD-check.yaml:53-56) defaults `error-on` to `"warning"`, so a test error is a hard check FAILURE on all five legs. By contrast the second live error, tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:33 (expects `regexp = "requires.*n_channels"`, gets the torch gate message), is genuinely local-only: `.moco_require_torch()` at R/foundation_moco.R:28-34 checks only `requireNamespace("torch")`, never `torch_is_installed()`, so with the R torch package present on CI the gate passes and the n_channels validation at R/foundation_weights.R:312-316 fires as the test expects.
findings.impact: The release documentation's central claim is unverifiable and most likely false. A CRAN submission driven by RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:19-21 (`devtools::submit_cran()`) would be rejected on the first auto-check. Worse, test-foundation-weights.R:29-37 is a test that is green only on CI and red locally, and 70 torch tests are green only locally and skipped on CI -- neither environment ever runs the full suite, so "the suite passes" has no single meaning in this project.
findings.action: Fix the underlying defect: either raise `num.trees` in tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:34 (and any sibling call) above ranger's OOB-quantile threshold, or have `.fit_core()` in R/active_fit.R:1-10 validate `num.trees` against `nrow(labeled)` and emit an edaphos-level error. Add `ranger (>= 0.18.0)` to DESCRIPTION Imports. findings.title: Shipped IV bundle refutes the README's "decisive test passes" headline: Sargan p = 3.2e-08, not 0.343
findings.correction: none on the core — I opened the bundle. inst/extdata/causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds carries version 3.10.0, date_computed "2026-04-27", used_real_stack TRUE, and benchmark_table rows: MAP 2SLS beta=0.007566, stage1_F=1494.93, sargan_p=3.2158e-08; Tree cover 2SLS beta=56.7052, F=14.80, sargan_p=7.468e-04; Clay 2SLS beta=-4.4644, F=2.686, sargan_p=8.857e-02 — over-identification rejects on 2 of 3. README.md:850-853 does publish 0.343/0.283/0.424 with ✅ under the header "v1.9.1 Sargan p (real MoCo)" and README.md:856-859 does declare "**The decisive test passes.** … the central empirical contribution of v1.9.1." data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R:66-71 confirms `means = rep(0, moco$n_channels), sds = rep(1, moco$n_channels)` fed to the real 31-channel stack, and its own comment concedes these stats are synthetic-mode values pending v1.9.2. Corroborators (b) β=56.7 g/kg per 1% tree cover and (c) the clay sign flip at F=2.69 hold. TWO WEAKENINGS: (a) the "53.3% exactly zero ⇒ saturated/dead-ReLU" inference is weak — ~50% zeros is textbook-normal for any ReLU embedding (the informative signal is the 3.29–465.86 magnitude range, not the cited "300-470"); and the vignette is less self-contradictory than claimed — vignettes/pilar1-pilar4-iv.Rmd:316/:346 ("Sargan p ≈ 10⁻⁹") is explicitly about the 27 *proxy* embeddings, a different instrument set, while the :419-428 transcript labels itself "no modo synthetic-stack". The undisputed fact remains: 05cb516 refreshed the bundle to a refutation and README.md:850-859 plus README.md:1626 and README.md:1700 ("Sargan passes empirically ✅") were never updated; README.md:1713 still marks v1.9.3 as 📝.
findings.evidence:
`README.md:850-859` publishes a table titled "v1.9.1 — Real MoCo v2 patch extraction passes the Sargan test" with `MAP → SOC | 0.343 ✅`, `Tree cover → SOC | 0.283 ✅`, `Clay → SOC | 0.424 ✅`, and concludes "**The decisive test passes.** ... This is the central empirical contribution of v1.9.1."

The artefact shipped in the package, `inst/extdata/causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds` (stamped `version = 3.10.0`, `date_computed = 2026-04-27`, `used_real_stack = TRUE`), contains `benchmark_table` with the opposite result:

```
2     MAP (mm/a) 2SLS (real MoCo v1)  beta=0.00757  stage1_F=1494.9  sargan_p=3.22e-08
4 Tree cover (%) 2SLS (real MoCo v1)  beta=56.7053  stage1_F=  14.8  sargan_p=7.47e-04
6       Clay (%) 2SLS (real MoCo v1)  beta=-4.4644  stage1_F=   2.69 sargan_p=8.86e-02
```

The over-identification test now **rejects** on 2 of 3 exposures. Three corroborating signs that the instruments are degenerate:
(a) `r$embedding_sample_first5_64` is 53.3% exactly zero, with non-zero entries in the 300-470 range — a saturated/dead-ReLU encoder. Cause is visible at `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R:66-71`, which feeds the real SoilGrids/WorldClim/SRTM stack through `dataset_meta` with `means = rep(0, moco$n_channels), sds = rep(1, moco$n_channels)` — i.e. **unnormalised**, against an encoder trained on z-scored tiles.
(b) Tree-cover 2SLS β = 56.7 g/kg per 1% tree cover (CI 29.7–83.7) implies 5670 g/kg SOC across 0→100% cover — physically impossible.
(c) Clay 2SLS β sign-flips vs OLS (−4.46 vs +0.195) at stage-1 F = 2.69, far below the Staiger–Stock threshold of 10.

The installed vignette carries the stale numbers as a hand-pasted, never-executed console transcript: `vignettes/pilar1-pilar4-iv.Rmd:424-428` inside an `eval = FALSE` chunk reads `#   2   MAP (mm/a) 2SLS (real MoCo v1) 0.01694  10.30  0.343  <- passa!`. The same vignette at line 316 states "**Todos os três estimadores 2SLS têm Sargan p ≈ 10⁻⁹**" and at line 346 "Sargan p permanece ≈ 0 para todos os k. Isso é uma assinatura clara de que os instrumentos são estruturalmente inválidos" — self-contradictory within one document.

Git history shows `05cb516 feat(v1.9.3): close roadmap promise -- IV refit with real 31-channel SoilGrids+WorldClim+SRTM stack` refreshed the bundle without updating the claim it refutes.
findings.impact: The package's self-declared "central empirical contribution" is asserted in the README and in a pkgdown-rendered vignette while the data shipped in the same tarball demonstrates the opposite. Any reviewer, rOpenSci editor, or citing author who opens `causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds` finds a refutation of the headline. Because the embeddings are saturated garbage from an unnormalised forward pass, neither the old "passes" nor the new "fails" number is scientifically meaningful — the entire Pillar 1 × Pillar 4 IV result is unsupported.
findings.action: 1. Fix the normalisation: persist the real per-channel training means/sds alongside the Zenodo encoder and pass them in `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R:66-71` instead of `rep(0)`/`rep(1)`. Assert `mean(emb == 0) < 0.1` and `max(abs(emb)) < 50` before proceeding. 2. Re-run at `target_res = 0.01` to match the encoder's training grid (the bundle records `stack_res_deg = 0.05`, and `vignettes/pilar1-pilar4-iv.Rmd:391` itself uses 0.01). 3. Rewrite `README.md:850-865` and `vignettes/pilar1-pilar4-iv.Rmd:416-428` to report whatever the re-run actually yields, and replace the pasted comment transcript with an evaluated chunk that reads the shipped bundle. 4. Add a test asserting the README's Sargan values against `inst/extdata/causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds`.
findings.resolution: The IV benchmark was re-run on real data and the headline was replaced by what the bundle actually shows, rather than hand-patched. The bundle was regenerated 2026-07-26 with normalisation_source recorded as aoi and a note that the v1 encoder's training statistics are unrecoverable.

findings.title: Every β in the README's real-data causal table disagrees with the shipped bundle, and the confounding correction has the wrong sign for tree cover
findings.evidence:
`README.md:626-641` "### Real-data results: 1095 Cerrado profiles" publishes:
```
| MAP (mm/a)     | naive 0.013 | adjusted 0.009 | confounding factor 1.5× |
| Tree cover (%) | naive 0.42  | adjusted 0.31  | confounding factor 1.4× |
| Clay (%)       | naive 0.38  | adjusted 0.25  | confounding factor 1.5× |
```
plus "a block-bootstrap sample (**B = 500**)".

Extracted from the shipped `inst/extdata/causal_cerrado_real.rds` (`edaphos_ver = 1.3.1`), `$effects[[x]]$lm`:
```
wc_bio_12           naive=0.00720039  adjusted=0.00709411  ratio=1.015  n_boot=200
wc_landcover_trees  naive=0.89786     adjusted=2.04791     ratio=0.438  n_boot=200
soilgrids_clay      naive=0.525729    adjusted=0.194894    ratio=2.698  n_boot=200
```
Not one of the six β values matches. The "confounding factor" column (1.5 / 1.4 / 1.5) versus actual (1.02 / 0.44 / 2.70) is wrong by 32x in the worst case. Critically, for tree cover the backdoor adjustment **more than doubles** the effect (0.898 → 2.048), whereas the README presents adjustment as uniformly shrinking an upward-confounded naive estimate. `B = 500` is contradicted by `length(effect_boot) == 200`.

The adjustment *sets* do match the bundle (MAP: 5 covariates, tree cover: 2, clay: 3), which rules out "different DAG" as an explanation — the numbers were simply never refreshed from the artefact.

A third value for the same MAP quantity appears at `README.md:877` (`effect = 0.00769`) and a fourth in `inst/extdata/causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds` row 1 (`Backdoor OLS beta = 0.0077766`).
findings.impact: The section that demonstrates the package's flagship Pillar 1 capability on real data reports numbers that exist nowhere in the repository, and reverses the sign of the scientific conclusion for one of three exposures. A reader who reproduces the analysis from `causal_cerrado_real.rds` — the documented way to do so — gets different answers with a different qualitative story. The uniform "≈1.5× confounding" pattern reads as fitted to the narrative rather than read off the data.
findings.action: Regenerate the `README.md:632-636` table programmatically from `inst/extdata/causal_cerrado_real.rds$effects` (via `README.Rmd` or an extension of `tools/make-readme-figures.R`) so it cannot drift again. Correct `B = 500` to 200 at `README.md:639` or re-run with B = 500. Reconcile the four different MAP β values across `README.md:634`, `README.md:877`, `causal_cerrado_real.rds`, and `causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds`. Rewrite the narrative to state that adjustment increases the tree-cover effect, which is a more interesting finding than the one currently claimed.
findings.resolution: The fabricated real-data causal table was replaced with measured results computed from a newly generated bundle, and the numbers are pinned by test.
