findings.title: foundation_weights_load() gates on torch before validating its own arguments — the live ERROR 2
findings.evidence:
R/foundation_weights.R:294 `.moco_require_torch()` is the FIRST statement of `foundation_weights_load()` (signature at :287-293). The pure-R argument validation that does not need torch at all is 15 lines later, :309-315: `if (is.null(n_channels) || is.null(feature_dim) || is.null(proj_dim)) stop("Loading from a local path requires `n_channels`, `feature_dim` and `proj_dim` to be supplied explicitly.", call. = FALSE)`.
`.moco_require_torch()` is defined at R/foundation_moco.R:28-34 and raises "Install the `torch` package to use foundation_moco_*()".
tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:28-37 asserts `expect_error(foundation_weights_load(f), regexp = "requires.*n_channels")` with NO skip gate — while the very next test at :39-40 does call `skip_if_no_torch()`. So the test author knew about the gate and missed this one block.
findings.impact: Two separate defects in one call: (1) a user who forgot `n_channels` is told to install a 1 GB dependency instead of being told which argument is missing — the opposite of the v3.8.0 friendly-error goal; (2) the test suite cannot go green on a torch-less machine, so the NEWS.md v3.10.0 claim of "R CMD check: 0 errors" cannot be reproduced by a reviewer without torch.
findings.action: Move `.moco_require_torch()` from R/foundation_weights.R:294 down to just before the first torch call, i.e. immediately above `EncCtor <- .moco_build_encoder()` at :326. That makes the argument validation at :309-315 reachable without torch and fixes the test with no test change. Independently, convert :311-315 to `.stopf(..., hint = "Read them from foundation_weights_list() or pass n_channels/feature_dim/proj_dim explicitly.")` for consistency with the other v3.8.0 entry points.
findings.resolution: foundation_weights_load("no-such-id") without torch now returns "Unknown pretrained encoder 'no-such-id'. Run foundation_weights_list() to see available names." -- the registry lookup runs before the torch gate.

findings.title: cran-comments.md is self-contradictory and every quantitative claim in it is stale or wrong
findings.correction: Almost everything holds, but the title's "every quantitative claim" is false and one sub-claim is REFUTED. Verified true: :20-21 "Status: OK / 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes" vs :69-70 "~13 MB" installed above the 5 MB soft cap (that IS the installed-size NOTE, so the two cannot both hold); :30-31 and :33-35 test/skip/warning claims all wrong; `causal_cerrado_real.rds` is 63,521 B = 62 KB vs the claimed 1.6 MB (26x); `du -sk inst/extdata` = 9780 KB vs "~8 MB"; the itemised list omits case_cerrado_results.rds (1,469,189 B), capstone_native_calibration.rds (758,948 B), capstone_campaign_results.rds (556,352 B), temporal_cerrado_results.rds (198,786 B); man/figures is 2364 KB and unmentioned; :4 R 4.5.3 vs local 4.6.1. NOT true: `benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds` is 1,959,632 B = 1.87 MB vs claimed 0.7 MB — that is 2.7x, not 26x (the 26x applies only to causal_cerrado_real.rds), and `benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds` at 4,640,252 B genuinely is ~4.5 MB as claimed. REFUTED: ":52 claims the base test suite runs without `Matrix` — but `Matrix::` is reached at 2 sites with only 1 `requireNamespace` guard." There is exactly one `Matrix::` *call* (R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:148) and it sits inside `if (requireNamespace("Matrix", quietly = TRUE))` at :147; :120 is a comment. cran-comments is correct about Matrix. Severity deflated from blocker: this is a ~20-minute prose/arithmetic fix in an .Rbuildignore'd file, embarrassing but code-neutral.
findings.evidence: The self-contradiction is gone - cran-comments.md is now generated by tools/status/render-cran-comments.R from a real check log, its status block is verbatim from tools/status/check.log, and the 0 notes line is replaced by the actual 2 NOTEs - but the finding's headline survives in a new form: the generated numbers are stale again. Its footer declares provenance at commit 35f385f, three commits behind HEAD, and bc59af8 shrank inst/extdata afterwards, so the quoted extdata 4.2Mb is now 2268 KB (2.2 MB) on disk; the test line says 2051 passing and 1 skipped where a live run gives 2095 pass and 14 skip; and the CRAN incoming section still reads Source tarball size: not measured. Regenerating the file closes this.
findings.impact: cran-comments.md is the first thing a CRAN volunteer reads. A file that contradicts itself in two adjacent sections and misstates file sizes by 26x invites a hostile review of everything else, and the claimed clean check will be trivially disproven by CRAN's own log.
findings.action: Delete the hand-written numbers. Run `R CMD check --as-cran` once, paste the verbatim tail of the log into `cran-comments.md`, and generate the size table with `du -b inst/extdata/* man/figures/*` rather than from memory. Drop the "0 notes" line and instead explain the (unavoidable) size NOTE.
findings.resolution: cran-comments.md was regenerated by tools/status/render-cran-comments.R from a fresh R CMD check log taken on an idle machine at commit 8e725b9, so every quantity in it is current: installed size 8.4Mb (doc 3.2, extdata 2.2) where it said 11.7Mb, 2 192 passing expectations across 92 test files where it said 2 051 across 88, and 5 unavailable Suggests named from the log. Its footer records the log's sha256 and the commit it was rendered at. tools/status/check-classification.json was stale in the same way and is corrected: it named a tarball at version 4.1.0 and '8 Suggests' while the package is 0.9.0 and the log names 5, and its own note explaining that counts are read from the log rather than stated had itself stated a count.

findings.title: Undeclared `utils` and `tools` namespaces — guaranteed R CMD check WARNING that cran-comments.md denies
findings.correction: Substance confirmed: DESCRIPTION:78-85 Imports = clhs, deSolve, httr2, jsonlite, ranger, Rcpp, stats (no utils, no tools); NAMESPACE's only import line is 245 `importFrom(Rcpp,evalCpp)`; every cited call site exists (causal_corpus.R:227, causal_kg_io.R:80/:370, causal_dag.R:316, causal_llm.R:378/:444/:320, causal_ontology.R:194, bridges_active_learning_v3.R:131/:220/:318, causal_active_learning.R:157, foundation_weights.R:111, foundation_embed_coords.R:226). `R CMD check` reports undeclared `::` imports as a WARNING, and cran-comments.md:19-22 asserts 0 warnings. Minor overcount: the raw greps return 35 utils:: / 11 tools:: lines, but several are roxygen or comments — the real *code* call sites are ~31 utils:: and 3 tools:: (foundation_weights.R:111, foundation_embed_coords.R:226, causal_llm.R:320). The WARNING fires regardless.
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:78-85` declares `Imports: clhs, deSolve (>= 1.40), httr2, jsonlite, ranger, Rcpp (>= 1.0.0), stats` — no `utils`, no `tools`. `NAMESPACE` imports nothing beyond `importFrom(Rcpp,evalCpp)` and `useDynLib(edaphos, .registration = TRUE)`.

R/ reaches into both via `::` anyway — 35 `utils::` sites and 8 `tools::` sites:
- `R/causal_corpus.R:227`  `collected <- utils::head(collected, max_results)`
- `R/causal_kg_io.R:80`, `:370`  `as.character(utils::packageVersion("edaphos"))`
- `R/causal_dag.R:316`  `utils::modifyList(bart_defaults, bart_kwargs)`
- `R/causal_llm.R:378`, `:444`  `utils::txtProgressBar` / `utils::setTxtProgressBar`
- `R/causal_ontology.R:194`  `utils::adist(...)`
- `R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:131`, `:220`, `:318` and `R/causal_active_learning.R:157`  `utils::head`
- `R/foundation_weights.R:111`  `tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache")`
- `R/foundation_embed_coords.R:226`  `cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache")`
- `R/causal_llm.R:320`  `as.character(tools::md5sum(tf))`

`R CMD check` emits `* checking dependencies in R code ... WARNING / '::' or ':::' import not declared from: 'tools', 'utils'`. `cran-comments.md:19-22` asserts `Status: OK / 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes`.
findings.impact: A WARNING (not a NOTE) on the CRAN incoming pipeline. Submissions with an unexplained WARNING are auto-rejected before a human reviewer sees them, and the cran-comments claim of a clean check is demonstrably false on the very first check section.
findings.action: Add `utils` and `tools` to `Imports` in DESCRIPTION (they are base-distribution packages, so this adds no install cost), then regenerate `cran-comments.md` from an actual `R CMD check --as-cran` log rather than from prose.
findings.resolution: DESCRIPTION Imports: clhs, deSolve (>= 1.40), httr2, jsonlite, ranger, Rcpp (>= 1.0.0), stats, tools, utils. The 'checking dependencies in R code' WARNING no longer appears in the check log.

findings.title: 134 of 169 exported functions have no examples; only 10 have an example R CMD check executes
findings.correction: none — reproduced exactly by cross-referencing NAMESPACE's 169 `export()` lines against `\alias{}`/`\examples` in all 182 man/*.Rd: 134 exports have no `\examples`; 36 of 182 Rd files have one; the 10 with a block R CMD check runs are exactly the named set (edaphos_posterior, causal_sensitivity_summary, piml_profile_fit, quantum_feature_map, predict.edaphos_piml_bayes, foundation_weights_list, llm_annotation_vocabulary, quantum_kernel, piml_profile_fit_bayesian, temporal_synth_soc_cube). bhs_fit, uncertainty_calibrate, dm_fit, dm_sample, gnn_fit, no_fno_fit, no_deeponet_fit, al_query, al_update, causal_estimate_effect, causal_adjustment_set, temporal_convlstm_fit, foundation_moco_pretrain, quantum_krr_posterior, edaphos_rmse/r2/picp all verified as exported with an Rd page and no examples. inst/rosc/submission.md:76-78 and :104 assert the opposite.
findings.evidence:
Cross-referencing `NAMESPACE` (169 `export()` lines) against `man/*.Rd` `\alias{}` blocks: **134 exports have no `\examples` section at all**. 146 of 182 Rd files have no `\examples`. Of the 36 files that do, 18 wrap the whole block in `\dontrun{}` and 8 in `\donttest{}` — leaving **10 exported functions with an example `R CMD check` actually runs**: `causal_sensitivity_summary`, `edaphos_posterior`, `foundation_weights_list`, `piml_profile_fit`, `piml_profile_fit_bayesian`, `predict.edaphos_piml_bayes`, `quantum_feature_map`, `quantum_kernel`, `temporal_synth_soc_cube`, `llm_annotation_vocabulary`.

The undocumented set includes every flagship entry point: `bhs_fit` (man/bhs_fit.Rd — has `\value`, `\description`, `\references`, no `\examples`), `uncertainty_calibrate` (man/uncertainty_calibrate.Rd — same), `dm_fit`, `dm_sample`, `gnn_fit`, `no_fno_fit`, `no_deeponet_fit`, `al_query`, `al_update`, `causal_estimate_effect`, `causal_adjustment_set`, `temporal_convlstm_fit`, `foundation_moco_pretrain`, `quantum_krr_posterior`, and all 10 `edaphos_*` metric helpers (`edaphos_rmse`, `edaphos_r2`, `edaphos_picp`, ...) which are pure numeric functions with no dependency excuse.

This is asserted false twice in the submission material: `inst/rosc/submission.md:76-78` — "**Examples**: every exported function has at least one `@examples` block" — and `:104` — "[x] All exported functions have Roxygen docs with `@return` and `@examples`."
findings.impact: "Please add small executable examples to your Rd files" is one of the most common CRAN first-round rejections, and rOpenSci review will not pass a package where 79% of the public API is unexercised by examples. The false self-report in inst/rosc/submission.md means the rOpenSci editor is misled in the pre-submission inquiry itself.
findings.action: Start with the ~40 exports that are pure and cheap (`edaphos_rmse/r2/mae/bias/picp/ece/interval_score/metrics_summary`, `dm_cosine_schedule`, `quantum_scale`, `quantum_hamiltonian*`, `causal_kg_*`, `gnn_build_graph`, `temporal_cube_to_tensor`) — these need 2-4 line examples on `br_cerrado` or synthetic data with no Suggests at all. Then add `\donttest{}` examples for `bhs_fit` and `uncertainty_calibrate` on a 50-row subset. Correct the two false claims in `inst/rosc/submission.md:76-78,104` before filing.
findings.resolution: NAMESPACE has 170 export() lines and 0 exports without an \examples block; 172 Rd files carry one, 129 of them outside \dontrun. The audit measured 134 of 169 exports with no example and 10 with a runnable one.

findings.title: Installed size will NOTE: inst/extdata 9.98 MB + man/figures 2.3 MB, of which a 1.9 MB PNG logo
findings.evidence: tools/status/check.log:31-36 records installed size is 11.7Mb with doc 4.5Mb, extdata 4.2Mb, help 1.5Mb. On disk at HEAD: du -sk inst/extdata = 2268 KB, man/figures = 716 KB.
findings.impact: `* checking installed package size ... NOTE` is unavoidable and will be the first thing quoted back. CRAN routinely rejects >10 MB first submissions outright pending justification, and the justification currently on file (cran-comments.md:67-96) misstates the sizes it is justifying.
findings.action: Three mechanical wins before touching the benchmark bundles: (1) re-encode `man/figures/logo.png` at 240px with `optipng`/`pngquant` — 1.9 MB to ~40 KB; (2) delete unreferenced `inst/extdata/llm_kg_smoke_claims.jsonl` and `man/figures/pillar4-foundation.png`; (3) re-save the five largest `.rds` with `saveRDS(..., compress = "xz")`. Then re-measure and rewrite the cran-comments size section from `du -b` output.
findings.resolution: The predicted NOTE does not fire and the arithmetic is stale in every term. R CMD check --as-cran at 7b881c2 reports 'checking installed package size ... INFO, installed size is 8.4Mb' -- under the 10Mb threshold that produces a NOTE. On disk: inst/extdata is 2.2 MB (the finding says 9.98 MB), man/figures is 0.7 MB (says 2.3 MB), and the '1.9 MB PNG logo' is 287 KB. The shrinking landed across bc59af8 and the vignette dpi reduction.

findings.title: The "v3.11.0" work is committed and self-referenced in shipped code, but no version exists: no DESCRIPTION bump, no NEWS section, no tag
findings.evidence: R/foundation_weights.R:82 edaphos_version = c(1.2.0, 4.0.0); DESCRIPTION:3 Version: 0.9.0; NEWS.md:1 is the sole heading, edaphos 0.9.0 (development version - not yet released).
findings.impact: `foundation_weights_list()` tells a user of edaphos 3.10.0 that a registry row requires edaphos 3.11.0, and `?foundation_build_cerrado_stack` documents behaviour "as of v3.11.0" -- a version that does not and may never exist. Anyone bisecting, citing, or reproducing HEAD has no version handle at all: HEAD is 16 commits of unnamed work, two of which (05cb516, 7400a2c) announce version numbers in their subject lines that appear nowhere in the package metadata. The v3.11.0 changes are therefore unreleasable as-is and unciteable.
findings.action: Decide the number once, then make it consistent in one commit: set DESCRIPTION:3 to `Version: 3.11.0`, prepend a `# edaphos 3.11.0` section to NEWS.md covering 05cb516 (31-channel IV refit), 7400a2c (MoCo v2 hand-off), 272b378 (MPS/CUDA resume fix), 01b7836 (covr workflow), 0adabef (governance docs), fd4ab0b (301-claim corpus), and tag it `git tag -a v3.11.0`. If v3.11.0 is not to be released, revert the v3.11.0 strings in R/foundation_weights.R:82, R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186,204,220 and re-roxygenise so man/ stops claiming a nonexistent version.
findings.resolution: R/foundation_weights.R stamped the unpublished edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2 with edaphos_version = '4.0.0', a version withdrawn as unreproducible and whose tag was deleted in the same commit, on an encoder that does not exist. It is NA now, matching every other field of that row that describes a publication which has not happened.

findings.title: Four mutually exclusive citation versions: DESCRIPTION 3.10.0, README 2.8.0, CITATION.cff 2.1.0, CITATION.cff preferred-citation 1.6.0
findings.correction: none — all four verified: DESCRIPTION:3 `Version: 3.10.0`; README.md:1727 "(Version 2.8.0)" and README.md:1734 `version = {2.8.0}`; CITATION.cff:109 `version: "2.1.0"` with :110 `date-released: "2026-04-23"`; preferred-citation `version: "1.6.0"`. `ls inst/CITATION` -> No such file. CITATION.cff:7 "organised across six research pillars" vs DESCRIPTION:8-9 "ten research pillars". Of 2.8.0 / 2.1.0 / 1.6.0 only v1.6.0 is a real tag (tag list ends v1.6.0 then jumps to v3.10.0).
findings.evidence: DESCRIPTION:3 `Version: 3.10.0`. README.md:1727 "Rodrigues, H. (2026). *edaphos ...* (Version 2.8.0) [Software]. Zenodo." and README.md:1734 bibtex `version   = {2.8.0}`. CITATION.cff:109 `version: "2.1.0"` with CITATION.cff:110 `date-released: "2026-04-23"`. CITATION.cff:184 `preferred-citation: ... version: "1.6.0"` -- i.e. the block CFF consumers prefer names a fifth-oldest release. `ls inst/CITATION` -> ABSENT, so `citation("edaphos")` falls back to DESCRIPTION and returns yet another answer (3.10.0), which README.md:1745-1747 actively directs users to ("An auto-generated citation is also available in R: `citation("edaphos")`"). CITATION.cff's abstract is also frozen: CITATION.cff:7 "It is organised across six research pillars" and the narrative stops at v2.1.0 (CITATION.cff:97-107), so the .cff describes a 6-pillar package while DESCRIPTION:8-9 describes a 10-pillar one.
findings.impact: GitHub renders the "Cite this repository" widget from CITATION.cff, so the repo's most prominent citation surface advertises v2.1.0 released 2026-04-23. Zenodo, Zotero, and rOpenSci tooling ingest the same file. A reader who cites via GitHub gets 2.1.0, via README gets 2.8.0, via `citation()` gets 3.10.0, via a CFF parser honouring preferred-citation gets 1.6.0. None of 2.8.0, 2.1.0 or 1.6.0 corresponds to a resolvable git ref except 1.6.0. This is unfixable after publication -- wrong versions propagate into other people's bibliographies.
findings.action: Make CITATION.cff the single source and derive it: set CITATION.cff:109 `version` and :110 `date-released` to the real release, delete or sync the redundant :184 `version` inside preferred-citation, refresh the :4-107 abstract to the 10-pillar description from DESCRIPTION:8-28, and update README.md:1727 and :1734 to the same number. Add a release-checklist step (or a CI job running `cffconvert --validate` plus a version-equality assertion against DESCRIPTION) so the four never drift again.
findings.resolution: Every artefact that states a version now states 4.1.0: DESCRIPTION, CITATION.cff (both the top-level field and preferred-citation), .zenodo.json, the README version badge and the top NEWS section. One distinct value across six artefacts, against the four mutually exclusive ones the audit found. Separately still true and still open: 4.1.0 has no git tag (last tag is v4.0.0) -- see FEA55C5.

findings.title: The "1 345 tests" figure is unreproducible, mis-attributed, and the NEWS test-count chain contains two arithmetic breaks
findings.correction: none — independently measured: 68 `test-*.R` files, 460 `test_that(` blocks, 1089 `expect_` calls, 75 `skip_if_not_installed(`. README.md:12 badge `tests-1345%20pass`, NEWS.md:72, cran-comments.md:30-35, inst/rosc/submission.md:69 all verified verbatim. Arithmetic breaks verified: NEWS.md:299 (3.6.0)=1274, NEWS.md:242 (3.7.0)=1282 but 1274+7=1281 (off by 1); NEWS.md:195 (3.8.0)=1308 but 1282+20=1302 (off by 6). The Ollama attribution is verified impossible: `grep -rn 'skip_on_cran|skip_if_offline|skip_on_ci' tests/testthat/` returns exactly one hit (test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46). Commit 4b15fb7 "fix(ci/windows): suppress cosmetic sweep() warning in test-pilar8-no-edge.R:42" exists in `git rev-list v3.10.0..HEAD`, confirming the blamed warning was already suppressed. README.md:1672 "**109+ unit and integration tests**" confirmed self-contradictory with the 1345 badge.
findings.evidence: Narrowed to one location, and that location is the document written for external reviewers and shipped into the user's library. inst/rosc/submission.md:68-69 still reads: Unit tests: 50+ test files, 1 345 expectations, and :79 still says 14 vignettes covering all 10 pillars (there are 19 in vignettes/). NEWS.md:326-331 explicitly withdraws the 1 345 figure, so submission.md is now the last surviving instance of it.
findings.impact: 1345 is defensible ONLY on a machine with torch, dagitty, bnlearn and dbarts installed (the 109 gated blocks would then execute and multiply into expectations) -- but that is nowhere stated, and no environment in the repo reproduces it. As published, the number is unverifiable by any reader and demonstrably wrong in the environment cran-comments.md itself designates as the base case. inst/rosc/submission.md:69's "50+ test files" understates 68, and calling 1345 "expectations" in one file and "unit tests" in another means the project does not know which quantity it is quoting.
findings.action: Pick one measured quantity and state the environment with it, e.g. "460 test_that blocks / 1089 expectations; 1022 pass + 109 skipped without torch/dagitty/bnlearn/dbarts (R 4.6.1 aarch64-darwin)". Regenerate the README.md:12 badge from that number, delete or correct the contradictory README.md:1672 "109+", fix the +7/+20 arithmetic at NEWS.md:242 and NEWS.md:195, and rewrite cran-comments.md:30-35 to report the true skip count and the true warning source (test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61, not Pilar 8 sweep).
findings.resolution: The 1 345 figure is gone from its last surviving location. inst/rosc/submission.md's test and vignette counts are generated from a real run (2 192 expectations, 92 test files, 19 vignettes), and tests/testthat/test-submission-claims.R fails if the withdrawn figure is asserted again -- while allowing it to be disclosed, since the generated block names it to say it was false.

findings.title: The README's only install command pins a git ref that does not exist (`@v2.8.0`)
findings.evidence: README.md:339-340: `remotes::install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos@v2.8.0", build_vignettes = TRUE)`. `git rev-parse -q --verify v2.8.0` -> not found (see the tag list: tags stop at v1.6.0 then jump to v3.10.0). This is the sole install instruction in the 84 KB README (`grep -rn install_github` over the repo returns only README.md:339 and Dockerfile:67). Cross-check: NEWS.md:805 documents a `# edaphos 2.8.0` release and the roadmap row README.md:1713 marks v2.8.0 as shipped -- so the pin is not a typo, it points at a release the project believes it made but never tagged.
findings.impact: Every new user's first command fails with `Error: Failed to install 'edaphos' from GitHub: reference 'v2.8.0' not found`. The package is effectively uninstallable by its documented path. It also silently pins users two major-minor arcs behind (2.8.0 vs 3.10.0) even if the tag were created.
findings.action: Change README.md:339 to install the current release (`edaphos@v3.10.0`, once #2 is resolved) or drop the pin entirely (`install_github("HugoMachadoRodrigues/edaphos", build_vignettes = TRUE)`). Add a CI step or a pre-release checklist item that greps README.md for `@v[0-9]` and verifies the ref resolves.
findings.resolution: Commit 2984aa5 unpinned the README install command, so it no longer points at a git ref that does not exist.

findings.title: CITATION.cff assigns the identical DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19710162 to twelve different "Version DOI" entries
findings.evidence: CITATION.cff:122-157 declares `type: doi, value: "10.5281/zenodo.19710162"` twelve times, labelled "Version DOI (v1.6.0)", "(v1.7.0)", "(v1.7.1)", "(v1.7.2)", "(v1.8.0)", "(v1.8.1)", "(v1.8.2)", "(v1.9.0)", "(v1.9.1)", "(v1.9.2)", "(v2.0.0)", "(v2.1.0)". Only two distinct DOIs appear besides it: :118 concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19683708 and :121 "Version DOI (v1.5.0)" 10.5281/zenodo.19709560. Zenodo mints a unique version DOI per deposit, so a single id cannot be the version DOI of twelve versions -- meaning eleven of these entries are fabricated, and (consistent with #2) no Zenodo deposit was ever made for v1.7.0 onward.
findings.impact: Anyone resolving 10.5281/zenodo.19710162 expecting v2.1.0 lands on whatever single record it actually is (v1.6.0/v1.7.0-era at best). The identifiers block makes the archival record look complete when eleven of thirteen versions were never archived. This is exactly the kind of provenance defect an rOpenSci reviewer or a journal data-availability check catches.
findings.action: Delete the eleven duplicate entries at CITATION.cff:125-157, keeping only DOIs that resolve (:118 concept, :121 v1.5.0, and whichever single record 19710162 really is, correctly labelled). Add real version DOIs only after each Zenodo deposit is actually published -- which per RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71 has not happened for v3.10.0.
findings.resolution: Commit 2984aa5 deleted the eleven duplicate version-DOI entries and wrote the reason into the file instead of leaving it implicit.

findings.title: DESCRIPTION promises ten research pillars; every document shipped in the CRAN tarball documents six, and pillars 7-10 have no roadmap row, no README section and no vignette
findings.evidence: DESCRIPTION:8-25 enumerates ten pillars. Against that: `R/pillars_roadmap.R:1` is titled "Roadmap and status of the six pillars of edaphos" and its table (lines 8-15) has exactly 6 rows; the generated `man/edaphos-roadmap.Rd:5` inherits that title. `R/edaphos-package.R:10,14` say "**six research pillars**" / `@section Six research pillars:`, rendered into `man/edaphos-package.Rd:13,20`. README.md:371 heading is `## The six pillars at a glance` and its table has 6 pillar rows plus 2 non-pillar rows; there is no `## Pillar 7/8/9/10` section (README pillar headings stop at :1288 `## Pillar 6 — Quantum ML`). `vignettes/` contains pilar1..pilar6 Rmd files only — no pilar7/8/9/10 vignette. README.md:10 badge reads `pillars-10%2F10%20shipped` and links to `#the-six-pillars-at-a-glance`. What DOES cover 7-10: `_pkgdown.yml:161-180` (four reference groups), `cheatsheets/pilar7.md`..`pilar10.md`, `vignettes/getting-started.Rmd:135-183`, `INTRO.md:42-59`, and man pages `bhs_fit.Rd`, `no_fno_fit.Rd`, `no_deeponet_fit.Rd`, `dm_fit.Rd`, `dm_sample.Rd`, `gnn_build_graph.Rd`, `gnn_fit.Rd`. Note `.Rbuildignore` excludes `^cheatsheets$`, `^INTRO\.md$`, `^_pkgdown\.yml$` — so of the artifacts covering 7-10, only getting-started.Rmd and the .Rd pages reach a CRAN user.
findings.impact: A CRAN reviewer reading DESCRIPTION then `?edaphos-package` or `?edaphos-roadmap` sees a direct contradiction (ten vs six) inside the tarball itself — a likely rOpenSci/CRAN comment. Users of pillars 7-10 get man pages with no narrative: no derivation vignette in the style promised at README.md:384-388 ("one or more vignettes deriving the object from first principles"), and no status/governing-object row in the roadmap landing page the docs designate as the API entry point.
findings.action: Four concrete gaps to close: (1) add rows 7-10 to the `R/pillars_roadmap.R` table and retitle to "ten pillars", then re-roxygenise; (2) change `R/edaphos-package.R:10,14` to ten and add \item blocks for pillars 7-10 mirroring the existing 1-6; (3) add `## Pillar 7`..`## Pillar 10` sections to README.md after :1288 and expand the at-a-glance table to 10 rows (also fix the anchor in the badge at :10); (4) promote at least `cheatsheets/pilar7.md`-`pilar10.md` content into real vignettes, or explicitly state in the roadmap that 7-10 are documented via cheatsheets + getting-started only.
findings.resolution: vignettes/ has 18 Rmd files including pilar7-bayesian-hierarchical, pilar8-neural-operators, pilar9-diffusion-models and pilar10-graph-attention; README carries a section for each of pillars 7-10; R/pillars_roadmap.R has a row for each and no longer calls itself the roadmap of six pillars. The related metadata claim, F545DD7, was open when this line was first written and was closed in the same session at a549528.

findings.title: R² is floored at zero in three benchmark code paths, censoring negative values and turning them into a "statistically indistinguishable" conclusion
findings.evidence: The code half is fixed and guarded - all three clamps are gone and R/quantum_foundation.R:469-478 now delegates to edaphos_rmse/edaphos_mae/edaphos_r2 with a comment at :464-468 explaining why - but the artefact was never regenerated, so the censored numbers are still what the package publishes. readRDS(inst/extdata/quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds) is still version 1.9.2, date_computed 2026-04-23, and its cv_summary r2_mean is exactly 0, 0, 0 for the three kernel methods against 0.0807 for ranger. README.md:1668-1678 prints those zeros and concludes that the four regressors are statistically indistinguishable - a conclusion the clamp manufactured.
findings.impact: A method that predicts worse than the training mean is published as "R² = 0.00", identical to a method that ties it. This directly underwrites the README's "statistically indistinguishable" and "matches but does not surpass ranger" conclusions and the NEWS "RMSE is a flat band" reading — conclusions drawn from a censored metric. Any reviewer recomputing R² from the stored predictions gets negative values that the package never reports.
findings.action: Remove `max(0, ...)` from all three sites and let R² go negative; a negative R² is the informative result. Re-run `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R`, `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R` and the quantum benchmark, and update `README.md:1406-1411`, `NEWS.md:601-608` and `NEWS.md:421-428`. Add a unit test that `benchmark`-family R² is not clipped (e.g. feed a constant predictor worse than the mean and assert the returned R² < 0).
findings.resolution: The bundle was regenerated by re-running data-raw/quantum_foundation_benchmark.R at HEAD with the unclamped edaphos_r2(). inst/extdata/quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds now holds 17 negative per-fold R2 values and zero exact zeros, where it previously held 17 exact zeros and no negatives; the run reproduces bit-for-bit from its seed. README.md and vignettes/pilar4-pilar6-quantum.Rmd were rewritten: the 'statistically indistinguishable' conclusion the clamp manufactured is replaced by the measured finding that all four methods, including the ranger baseline, fall below the null. The vignette's hand-typed '#>' console block -- indistinguishable from knitr output -- was replaced by a live chunk reading the bundle. tests/testthat/test-readme-numbers.R binds the table to the bundle and asserts no censored R2 survives.

findings.title: The v1.8.0 multi-backend LLM benchmark is entirely simulated and its headline F1/latency values are hard-coded function arguments
findings.correction: Verified end to end: inst/extdata/llm_benchmark_results.rds has `mode = "simulated"`, `version = 1.7.2`, `date_computed = 2026-04-23 16:52:56` (predating the v1.8.0 release it documents); data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R:128/:142/:156 carry the hard-coded `sim_args` exactly as quoted (latency_mean 15.2 / 3.1 / 5.7; precision_target 0.85 / 0.80 / 0.90); R/llm_benchmark.R:334-338 derives false positives analytically from `precision_target`, and :351-361 draws them iid from a shared 17-token `noise_pool`, so near-zero pairwise kappa is structural — the shipped `kappa_matrix` off-diagonals (-0.0811, 0.1216) match README's "κ ≈ −0.08 to 0.12" precisely. Two refinements: the tabulated P/R/F1 are simulator *outputs*, not the literal inputs (Claude prints precision 0.82 against a precision_target of 0.90), so "the reported values are inputs" overstates slightly; and README.md:697-700 does disclose the simulation — but four lines BELOW the table, framed as "runs reproducibly in CI", and without retracting "The first quantitative validation" or any of the "Key findings". Vendor-attributed numbers for three named commercial products remain unmeasured.
findings.evidence:
`README.md:668-695` presents "### v1.8.0 — Multi-backend LLM extraction benchmark ... **The first quantitative validation** of the Gemma 4 extractor" with a table of Precision / Recall / F1 / Cost / "Latency (median)" for Gemma 4, GPT-4o-mini and Claude Sonnet-4.5, followed by "**Key findings.**"

The shipped artefact `inst/extdata/llm_benchmark_results.rds` has `mode = "simulated"` and `version = 1.7.2` (`date_computed = 2026-04-23`, i.e. predating the v1.8.0 release it documents). No API was ever called.

The reported values are inputs, not measurements. `data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R`:
```
128:  sim_args = list(recall = 0.80, precision_target = 0.85, ... latency_mean = 15.2, latency_sd = 4.1)   # Gemma 4
142:  sim_args = list(recall = 0.88, precision_target = 0.80, ... latency_mean = 3.1,  latency_sd = 0.8)   # GPT-4o-mini
156:  sim_args = list(recall = 0.84, precision_target = 0.90, ... latency_mean = 5.7,  latency_sd = 1.4)   # Claude
```
and `R/llm_benchmark.R:327-338` shows `llm_benchmark_simulate(gold, recall = 0.82, precision_target = 0.86, ...)` derives false positives analytically from `precision_target`.

Each README "key finding" is therefore a restatement of an author-chosen constant:
- "**Claude has the best F1** (0.82)" ← Claude has the highest `precision_target` (0.90) by construction.
- "**GPT-4o-mini is the fastest** (2.8 s vs. 5.4 s vs. 16 s median latency per abstract)" ← `latency_mean = 3.1 / 5.7 / 15.2`; the seconds are draws from `rnorm`, not wall-clock timings.
- "**Backends disagree strongly on which abstracts to extract** (κ ≈ −0.08 to 0.12 pairwise), which means ... This finding **justifies the three-backend architecture** already shipped." ← false positives are drawn iid per backend from a shared `noise_pool` (`R/llm_benchmark.R:353-361`), so near-zero pairwise κ is a mathematical necessity of the simulator, not an empirical discovery.

The disclosure at `README.md:697-700` ("runs reproducibly in CI using `llm_benchmark_simulate()`") appears *after* the table and does not retract the "Key findings".
findings.impact: An architecture decision ("justifies the three-backend architecture") and a cost/quality tradeoff recommendation ("switching from Claude to Gemma 4 saves ~$37.50 at the cost of 11 F1-points") are presented as empirical results derived from a simulator whose per-backend parameters the author selected. Vendor-attributed performance numbers for three named commercial products, published in a citable package, are fabricated in the technical sense that no measurement was taken. This is the single highest-reputational-risk item in the repository.
findings.action: Either (a) run the real benchmark once with `EDAPHOS_USE_REAL_LLM=1`, commit the resulting `mode = "real"` bundle, and report those numbers; or (b) if a real run is out of scope, delete the vendor-named table from `README.md:676-695` entirely and replace it with a statement that the harness is validated on a deterministic simulator and carries no empirical vendor comparison. Do not keep vendor-attributed P/R/F1/latency figures sourced from `sim_args`. Add a guard in `data-raw/llm_benchmark_run.R` that refuses to write to `inst/extdata/` when `USE_REAL` is FALSE, or writes to a `*_simulated.rds` filename.
findings.resolution: The claim was withdrawn rather than faked, which is the correct half of the finding's own recommended action: the bundle still records mode = simulated and the README now says so in the heading and the body.

findings.title: No test validates any headline number or any of the twelve committed result bundles
findings.correction: Core claims CONFIRMED: only tests/testthat/test-llm-annotation.R:111 reads inst/extdata (the gold-standard JSONL); no .rds bundle is opened by any test; the headline-number grep hits only the comment at test-benchmark-6pilar.R:4; NEWS.md:357 "1 269 tests pass" and cran-comments.md:5 "0/0/0"; the Sargan divergence is real (README.md:852 "0.343 ✅" vs causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds benchmark_table$sargan_p[2] = 3.22e-08). One detail is wrong: there is no 0.2188 or "1095" match at test-llm-annotation.R:95 -- the grep returns exactly one hit repo-wide in tests/, the comment at test-benchmark-6pilar.R:4.
findings.evidence:
A grep for the published figures across the whole suite returns nothing: `grep -rn "13\.51|14\.07|13\.86|0\.2188|1095" tests/testthat/` matches only a comment (`tests/testthat/test-benchmark-6pilar.R:4`, "the full 1 095-profile run lives in") and an unrelated confidence value (`test-llm-annotation.R:95`).

Exactly **one** of 69 test files reads anything from `inst/extdata/`: `tests/testthat/test-llm-annotation.R:111` (`system.file("extdata", "cerrado_gold_standard_v1.jsonl", ...)`), and only to parse the gold-standard JSONL. None of the twelve `.rds` result bundles — `case_cerrado_results.rds`, `causal_cerrado_real.rds`, `causal_iv_cerrado_real.rds`, `benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds`, `quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds`, `llm_benchmark_results.rds`, and the rest — is opened by any test.

The consequence is demonstrable: the Sargan sign-flip (README 0.343 ✅ vs bundle 3.2e-08) survived commit `05cb516 feat(v1.9.3): close roadmap promise -- IV refit with real 31-channel ... stack`, whose entire purpose was to refit that analysis. Likewise every β in `README.md:632-636` drifted from `causal_cerrado_real.rds` undetected across ~30 releases. Meanwhile `NEWS.md:357` claims "1 269 tests pass" and `cran-comments.md:5` claims "0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes", so the suite's green status is actively reassuring about claims it never checks.
findings.impact: For a package whose product is its claims, the test suite covers the code but not the science. 1022 passing expectations provide no protection against the exact failure mode that has already occurred three times (IV Sargan, causal β table, LLM benchmark mode). Any future refit will silently desynchronise the README again.
findings.action: Add `tests/testthat/test-headline-claims.R` that loads each `inst/extdata/*.rds` and asserts the values quoted in `README.md` and `NEWS.md` to the published precision — Sargan p-values, the six causal β, the 6-pillar RMSE/R²/PICP/CRPS aggregate, the case-study RMSE/MAE/R²/PICP, and `mode == "real"` for `llm_benchmark_results.rds`. Also assert artefact provenance: `as.character(r$version) == "3.10.0"` (or an explicit allow-list of intentionally frozen artefacts) so staleness surfaces as a test failure. Best of all, generate the README tables from the bundles via `README.Rmd` so drift becomes structurally impossible.
findings.resolution: A claim-binding test layer was added across the campaign, so headline numbers and shipped bundles are now asserted against each other rather than published unchecked.

findings.title: `.bench_inject_aleatoric()` manufactures the published PICP with author-chosen noise and silently degrades the published RMSE
findings.correction: none — verified end to end. R/benchmark_wosis.R:24-34 states the intent and the 0.20→0.85 target verbatim; :35-41 is the injector; call sites are :126 (P1), :184 (P6), :254 (P10); `.bench_residual_sd` at :47-52 is applied to in-sample fits (`stats::fitted(full_lm)` at :125). NEWS.md:386-389 reports PICP 0.232→0.953 / 0.249→0.601 / 0.073→0.825 and NEWS.md:430-433 concedes the in-sample no-LOO estimator. The RMSE corruption is arithmetically confirmed against the shipped bundle: `posterior_bank[[6]]$p1$metadata$sigma_resid` = 15.19607, `cv_aggregate` gives P10 rmse_mean = 15.19945 against NEWS.md:605's pre-injection 14.07, and sqrt(15.199² − 14.07²) = 5.75 ≈ sigma_resid/sqrt(n_ensemble=8) (data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:124), exactly the predicted colMeans residual offset; P1 with n_boot = 300L (:97) moves only 13.94→13.92 as predicted. P10's R² is 0.000 and it falls from rank 3 (NEWS.md:605-607, tied 14.07) to rank 6 in the re-sorted v3.4.0 table. NEWS.md:391-395 advertises only the CRPS gains; the RMSE regression appears in the :421-428 table but is never named. Severity honest: this is the package's own head-to-head, three of six methods affected, and it changes the ranking that data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:194 presents.
findings.evidence:
`R/benchmark_wosis.R:24-41` documents the intent explicitly: "v3.4.0 adds the missing ALEATORIC term: an estimate of the in-sample residual standard deviation `sigma_resid` is injected as iid Gaussian noise on every (sample, test-row) entry of the posterior matrix ... **PICP at the v3.1.0 head-to-head settings moves from ~0.20 to ~0.85, matching P4/P5/P7.**"

```r
35: .bench_inject_aleatoric <- function(pred_mat, sigma_resid, seed = NULL) {
37:   if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed + 13579L)
38:   noise <- matrix(stats::rnorm(length(pred_mat), 0, sigma_resid), nrow(pred_mat), ncol(pred_mat))
40:   pred_mat + noise
```
Called at `:126` (P1), `:184` (P6), `:254` (P10). `sigma_resid` comes from `.bench_residual_sd()` (`:47-52`) applied to **in-sample training** residuals.

Two distinct defects:

**(a) Coverage is set, not measured.** `NEWS.md:384-389` reports PICP_90 jumping "to nominal coverage": P1 0.232→0.953, P6 0.249→0.601, P10 0.073→0.825. `NEWS.md:430-433` concedes "P1 PICP is now mildly OVER-covered (0.95 vs nominal 0.90) because the OLS residual SD is computed in-sample without a leave-one-out adjustment". The published PICP is therefore a function of an undisclosed estimator choice, not a property of the model.

**(b) The injected noise corrupts the point predictions and thus RMSE/R².** Point predictions are `colMeans(post$samples)` (`data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:153`). Averaging `n` rows of injected noise leaves a residual offset of sd `sigma_resid/sqrt(n)`. Verified against the shipped bundle: `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds$posterior_bank[[6]]$p1$metadata$sigma_resid = 15.196`. With `n_ensemble = 8L` for P10 (`data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:124`), the injected error is ≈15.2/√8 ≈ 5.4 g/kg — and the bundle's `cv_aggregate` shows **P10 RMSE = 15.199** against `NEWS.md:605`'s pre-injection **14.07** (sqrt(14.07² + 5.66²) = 15.17 ✓). P1, with `n_boot = 300L`, moves only 13.94 → 13.92 as predicted (15.2/√300 = 0.88). P10's R² is driven to exactly 0.000 and it drops from rank 3 to rank 6 in the re-sorted table (`NEWS.md:421-428`), with `NEWS.md:391-395` advertising only "CRPS also improves materially across the board" and no mention of the RMSE regression it caused.
findings.impact: Three of the six methods in the package's 6-pillar head-to-head have their calibration metric manufactured and their accuracy metric degraded by a fixed-seed noise draw. A reader comparing PICP across the six methods is comparing a real QRF quantile grid (P4/P5) against three numbers tuned to sit near 0.90. The reported P10 RMSE of 15.20 is 8% worse than the model's actual out-of-sample error purely because of the injection, which materially changes the ranking that `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:194` (`arrange(rmse_mean)`) presents.
findings.action: Stop mutating the posterior samples. Instead (1) estimate the aleatoric term out-of-sample — CV residuals or a leave-one-out/OOB adjustment, not `stats::sd` of in-bag residuals; (2) widen the *intervals* analytically (convolve the epistemic spread with the aleatoric variance when computing PICP/MPIW/CRPS) so the point prediction is untouched and RMSE/R² are unaffected; (3) report both the epistemic-only and total-uncertainty PICP side by side; (4) in `NEWS.md:415-433` disclose the P10 RMSE regression from 14.07 to 15.18 as a consequence of the change rather than presenting only the CRPS improvement.
findings.resolution: Both defects fixed: the author-chosen aleatoric noise injection is gone and the RMSE degradation it caused was corrected, with the response scale made honest in the same pass.

findings.title: The P4 "Foundation" row of the headline "first honest cross-pillar comparison" is computed on a pure Gaussian-noise raster
findings.correction: none — every cited line verified in data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R: the template raster is filled with `stats::rnorm(terra::ncell(tpl))` and every one of the 31 encoder channels is overwritten with `stats::rnorm` in the following loop (the script's own message even prints "synthetic stack"); `dataset_meta` normalisation is `means = rep(0, ...), sds = rep(1, ...)`; `train_bhs <- if (n_tr > 300L) train[sample(n_tr, 300L), ] else train` caps P7 at 300 rows while P4/P5 get the full training fold; and the P7 "posterior" is rebuilt as `stats::rnorm(200L, pr$mean[j], pr$sd[j])`. README.md:243-255 carries no caveat, in direct contrast to README.md:1404/:1413 which does label the quantum table "(synthetic-stack mode)" / "random Gaussian rasters". The propagation into the 6-pillar table is consistent with the shipped benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds reusing the same P4/P5/P7 rows.
findings.evidence: The headline defect is fixed - data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R:193-230 now builds the real 31-channel stack via foundation_build_cerrado_stack(bbox, target_res = 0.01, schema = v1_encoder), with :200-205 recording that through v3.10.0 this benchmark ran the encoder over pure rnorm noise - and the 300-row P7 cap is now an opt-in env var (P7_TRAIN_CAP at :270-272, unset by default). One cited sub-defect survives verbatim and undisclosed: :183-186 still discards the Gibbs posterior and rebuilds it as samps[, j] <- stats::rnorm(200L, pr$mean[j], pr$sd[j]), so P7's CRPS and PICP still measure a Gaussian approximation of a summary. README.md:359 discloses the old noise raster but nothing discloses this reconstruction.
findings.impact: The result advertised as the package's "first honest cross-pillar comparison" attributes a calibration win to a foundation model that was fed noise, and awards R²/MPIW honours to a method trained on 34% of the data whose posterior was replaced by a Gaussian. Because `data-raw/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.R:59-62,179,210` reuses this bundle wholesale for the P4/P5/P7 rows, the defect propagates into the 6-pillar table in `NEWS.md:601-608` and `NEWS.md:421-428` and into `inst/extdata/benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds`.
findings.action: Either supply the real 31-channel Cerrado stack (the same one `data-raw/causal_iv_benchmark_real.R` builds via `foundation_build_cerrado_stack()`) with correct per-channel normalisation, or drop the P4 row and state that Pillar 4 is not benchmarkable without the raster download. Equalise P7's training set with P4/P5 or disclose the 300-row cap in every table caption. Replace the `rnorm(200, mean, sd)` reconstruction at `:139-144` with the actual Gibbs draws from `bhs_fit`. Add a "synthetic-stack mode" caveat to `README.md:243-255` matching the one already at `README.md:1404`.
findings.resolution: predict.edaphos_bhs() now returns the sampler's own predictive draws under draws = TRUE (as an attribute, so no existing caller changes), and data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R uses them instead of rebuilding rnorm(200, mean, sd) from the summary. The cost of the substitution is measured rather than asserted: a paired diagnostic scores both distributions over the same predictions, fold and held-out truth, with the Gaussian drawn on a private RNG stream. On this archive it was CRPS 0.3405 vs 0.3420 and PICP90 0.9224 vs 0.9283 against a nominal 0.90; the per-fold table ships in the bundle as p7_gaussian_gap. The correction was propagated through benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds, the README pooled table and the rendered manuscript.

findings.title: edaphos-cerrado-moco-v2 ships as an all-NA placeholder row in the exported public registry, keyed to a nonexistent package version 3.11.0
findings.evidence: The v2 registry row is still an all-NA placeholder in an exported function: R/foundation_weights.R:67 (url), :71 (sha256), :75 (doi) and :80 (published_at) are NA_character_ with the same filled-after-the-Zenodo-upload comments, and two further fields, norm_stats_url (:95-96) and norm_stats_status (:98-101), are NA and pending. The nonexistent version it is keyed to changed number rather than going away: :82 is now edaphos_version = c(1.2.0, 4.0.0) against DESCRIPTION:3 Version: 0.9.0.
findings.impact: `foundation_weights_list()` is an exported catalogue documented (R/foundation_weights.R:87-100) as describing "every pretrained encoder published by the `edaphos` project". Half its rows describe an artefact that does not exist, with a `license = "CC-BY-4.0"` and a full hyperparameter spec that make it look publishable. Users reading the table, or scripting over it, cannot distinguish published from aspirational except by NA-checking four columns. The `edaphos_version = "3.11.0"` column tells a user the weights need a package release that is not on CRAN, GitHub, or in NEWS.
findings.action: Either (a) drop the v2 row from `.foundation_weights_registry()` until the Zenodo deposit exists and re-add it in the release that publishes it, or (b) add an explicit `status` column (`"published"` / `"pending"`) so the placeholder is machine-readable, document it in the `@return` block at R/foundation_weights.R:100, and change `edaphos_version` to the version that will actually ship it. Separately, replace the v3.11.0 references in R/foundation_embed_coords.R:186,204,220 with 3.10.0 and re-roxygenise so man/foundation_build_cerrado_stack.Rd stops advertising a nonexistent release.
findings.resolution: The moco-v2 registry row is labelled NOT PUBLISHED and no longer quotes an expected InfoNCE loss. It had cited '~0.4 expected' beside v1's measured '~1.64', which reads as two numbers of equal standing when one is a measurement and the other a hope; no loss is stated until one is measured. The accessors were already honest -- foundation_weights_download() and _load() refuse with an explicit 'no published URL yet' message rather than failing obscurely -- so the defect was the description, not the behaviour.

findings.title: foundation_build_cerrado_stack() silently writes a truncated stack to the cache when any geodata fetch fails, then reuses it forever
findings.evidence: Half fixed. The build path now asserts the channel count: .stack_expected_layers() at R/foundation_embed_coords.R:309 and the guard at :625-633 stop before writing when the fetched layer count does not match the schema. The cache-hit path is untouched and it is the half the title names: :495-498 still does if (!force && file.exists(stack_path)) { message(Using cached stack); return(terra::rast(stack_path)) } with no terra::nlyr() check, so any short stack already written under a schema-keyed filename is still returned forever with only an informational message.
findings.impact: A transient WorldClim outage during the first call yields a 7-layer stack (5 SoilGrids + 2 SRTM) cached under the filename `cerrado_stack_v1_encoder_<hash>.tif`, which claims to be the v1_encoder schema. Every subsequent call returns that poisoned cache with only an informational "Using cached stack" message -- `force = TRUE` is the only escape and the user has no signal they need it. Feeding it to the 31-channel v1 encoder produces a torch conv2d channel-mismatch error far from the cause; feeding it to any user code that indexes layers positionally silently reads the wrong covariate. The docstring at :202-204 says this rewrite exists specifically to stop the IV benchmark falling back to a synthetic stack, so a silently-truncated real stack is the exact failure mode it was built to prevent.
findings.action: After line 361 in R/foundation_embed_coords.R, assert the schema's channel count before writing: `expected <- if (schema == "v1_encoder") 31L else 10L; if (terra::nlyr(stk) != expected) stop(sprintf("schema '%s' expects %d layers but only %d could be fetched (%s). Re-run when the sources are reachable.", schema, expected, terra::nlyr(stk), paste(names(layers), collapse=", ")))`. Also convert the five `message("      [warn] ", ...)` calls to `warning(...)` so partial failures are visible to `withCallingHandlers` and to test suites, and validate `terra::nlyr()` on the cache-hit path at line 245 before returning.
findings.resolution: The cache-hit path in foundation_build_cerrado_stack() now validates the cached raster against the schema before returning it, checking layer NAMES as well as count -- a count-only check passes a stack with the right number of wrong layers. An entry that fails falls through to a rebuild rather than raising, because a corrupt cache entry should be replaced, and if the sources are still unreachable the existing build guard names the missing layers. The decision lives in .cached_stack_ok() so it can be tested without the network: rejecting a cache entry falls through to a rebuild, and a rebuild needs every remote source, which is not a thing a unit test should require to prove a two-layer file is not a thirty-one-layer stack.

findings.title: qf_krr_benchmark() clamps R-squared at zero, contradicting the package's own edaphos_r2() and hiding worse-than-mean quantum models
findings.correction: Confirmed and stronger than argued. R/quantum_foundation.R:279 `r2 = max(0, 1 - ...)` is the only `max(0, 1 -` in R/; edaphos_r2 (R/edaphos_metrics.R:63-70) is unclamped and its header at :7-10 documents it as Nash-Sutcliffe. New evidence the auditor did not have: the clamp demonstrably fired in the SHIPPED bundle. `inst/extdata/quantum_foundation_cerrado.rds$cv_table` has `r2 == 0.00000000` in 9 of the 12 rows I inspected — in fold 2, RBF-KRR (RMSE 9.57) and ranger (RMSE 13.51) both report 0.00 despite a 4 g/kg RMSE gap, i.e. the clamp erased a real ordering. That bundle is what README.md:1406-1411 prints (0.00 for three of four methods) under the conclusion "The four regressors are statistically indistinguishable on this benchmark" — a conclusion the clamp manufactures.
findings.evidence:
R/quantum_foundation.R:274-283, the local `metrics()` helper used for every row of the benchmark table:
```r
r2     = max(0, 1 - sum(err^2, na.rm = TRUE) /
                    sum((truth - mean(truth, na.rm = TRUE))^2)),
```
The package's canonical metric does the opposite -- R/edaphos_metrics.R:63-69 returns the unclamped value, guarding only the degenerate case:
```r
edaphos_r2 <- function(observed, predicted) {
  ...
  if (ss_tot == 0) return(NA_real_)
  1 - ss_res / ss_tot
}
```
and documents itself at R/edaphos_metrics.R:7-10 as "Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency when the mean is the trivial model" -- a quantity whose whole diagnostic value is that it goes negative. `grep -rn "max(0, 1 -" R/*.R` returns exactly one hit, R/quantum_foundation.R:279, so this is a lone deviation, not a house style.
findings.impact: `qf_krr_benchmark()` is documented (R/quantum_foundation.R:247-250) as giving "an empirical answer" to whether the quantum-foundation hybrid beats its ancestors, and it tabulates the quantum KRR head-to-head against a ranger baseline. Clamping at 0 means a quantum model with true R-squared of -0.4 (materially worse than predicting the mean) is reported as 0.00, indistinguishable from a model that merely explains nothing. The clamp applies to every row including the baselines, so it compresses exactly the region where the comparison would be most informative. This directly undercuts the "Honestly benchmarked" claim the package makes about its Pillar 4/6 comparisons (R/pillars_roadmap.R:13).
findings.action: Replace the inline computation at R/quantum_foundation.R:277-281 with calls to the existing `edaphos_rmse()` / `edaphos_mae()` / `edaphos_r2()` so the benchmark shares one metric definition with the rest of the package, removing the `max(0, ...)`. Add a test asserting that a deliberately bad predictor yields a negative `r2` in the returned data frame.
findings.resolution: The R-squared clamp was removed and the function now delegates to the package's own metrics, so worse-than-mean quantum models are reported as negative rather than censored to zero.

findings.title: bhs_fit has no rank check on the model matrix: a constant covariate yields NA rgamma rates (the 2 live WARNINGs) then a cryptic Cholesky death
findings.correction: Mechanism and every behavioural claim CONFIRMED: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 seeds beta from stats::lm.fit (NA on rank-deficient X), the NA reaches rate_s at :302 -> rgamma at :303 and rate_t at :308 -> :309 (exactly the 2 live warnings), validation at :90-106 never checks rank(X), and test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 is a tautology (`expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` at :68). Two line references are wrong: `rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2` is at :283, not :288 (:288 is the w_cur draw); `.chol_jitter` is defined at :246-256 with the heavy-ridge fallback at :255, not :243-254. The tryCatch spans :61-65, not :61-66.
findings.evidence: Reproduced standalone (no package load) for n=30, X = cbind(1, rep(1,30)): `qr(X)$rank = 1` vs `p = 2`; `stats::lm.fit(X,y)$coefficients` = c(0.1327746, NA). R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 uses exactly that as the Gibbs initial value: `beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)`. The NA propagates: :288 `rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2` -> all NA -> :302 `rate_s` NA -> :303 `sigma2 <- 1/stats::rgamma(1, shape=shape_s, rate=NA)` emits WARNING "NAs produced" and returns NaN; :308-309 does the same for tau2 -> WARNING #2. Exactly two warnings, matching the live run at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61. On iteration 2 `prec_w` is all-NaN, the 8-step jitter ladder in `.chol_jitter` (:243-254) fails every try, and the final fallback `chol(M + diag(1e-2 * mean(diag(M))))` errors with "the leading minor of order 1 is not positive" (verified). The test at test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 swallows this with `tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL)` at :61-66 and then asserts the tautology `expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` at :68 -- satisfied by both branches, so it can never fail. Also note bhs_fit's own validation (:90-106) checks data/formula/coords types and the MCMC schedule but never the rank of X. R/core_utils.R already ships `.stopf` / `.assert_type` for exactly this.
findings.impact: Any user whose design matrix is rank-deficient (a constant covariate, a perfectly collinear pair, a one-level factor after NA dropping) gets 'NAs produced' followed by 'the leading minor of order 1 is not positive' -- with no indication which column is at fault -- from the Pillar 7 flagship sampler. The only test covering the case is a tautology, so the suite records it as passing while emitting the warnings that R CMD check will surface.
findings.action: In R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R after line 130 (`n <- length(y); p <- ncol(X)`) add a rank guard using the existing helper: `if (qr(X)$rank < p) .stopf("design matrix is rank-deficient (rank %d < %d columns).", qr(X)$rank, p, hint = "Drop constant or collinear covariates; aliased column(s): ...")`, naming the aliased columns from `colnames(X)[is.na(stats::lm.fit(X,y)$coefficients)]`. Then rewrite tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 as `expect_error(bhs_fit(...), "rank-deficient")` and wrap it in `expect_no_warning()` so the 2 'NAs produced' warnings become a regression signal instead of noise.
findings.resolution: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R now computes qr(X)$rank and names the aliased columns; the rank-deficient fit raises one informative error and zero warnings, against the 2 warnings the audit measured.

findings.title: R/foundation_finetune.R:41 makes the whole Pillar-4 fine-tuning API require `reticulate`, which it never uses
findings.correction: none — verified exactly. R/foundation_finetune.R:40-46 is `.ft_require_torch <- function() { if (!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) || !requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install the `torch` package (and its MPS / CUDA backend) to use the fine-tuning API.", call. = FALSE) }`; `grep -n reticulate R/foundation_finetune.R` returns the single hit at :41 in a 646-line file; the guard is called at :247, :401, :483, :632 (the four public entry points); reticulate is Suggests-only (DESCRIPTION:64). The masking is confirmed too: tests/testthat/test-foundation-finetune.R:7-12 defines a local `skip_if_no_torch()` that checks only `skip_if_not_installed("torch")` + `torch::torch_is_installed()`, never reticulate, so no test can ever reach the reticulate branch. Severity is honest: a torch-installed, reticulate-free R user — the normal case — gets four documented entry points dead behind an error message that tells them to install what they already have.
findings.evidence: R/foundation_finetune.R:40-46: `.ft_require_torch <- function() { if (!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) || !requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install the `torch` package (and its MPS / CUDA backend) to use the fine-tuning API.", call. = FALSE) }`. Line 41 is the ONLY occurrence of the string `reticulate` in the entire 646-line file (`grep -n reticulate R/foundation_finetune.R` -> single hit). The four call sites are the four public entry points: foundation_fit_classifier (guard at :247, defined :233), predict.edaphos_foundation_classifier (:401 / :397), foundation_fit_regressor (:483 / :468), predict.edaphos_foundation_regressor (:632 / :630). `reticulate` is Suggests-only (DESCRIPTION). The bug is masked by the test gate: tests/testthat/test-foundation-finetune.R:7-12 `skip_if_no_torch()` checks only torch + torch_is_installed(), never reticulate, so all 8 blocks in that file skip rather than fail on a torch-full/reticulate-free machine.
findings.impact: On a machine with torch and libtorch correctly installed but no reticulate (the normal case for an R-only user), all four fine-tuning entry points die with an error message that tells the user to install torch -- which they already have. Unfixable by the user without reading the source. Zero tests can catch it.
findings.action: Delete `!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) ||` from R/foundation_finetune.R:41. Add a torch-free regression test that stubs `requireNamespace` (or uses `local_mocked_bindings`) to assert `.ft_require_torch()` does not consult reticulate.
findings.resolution: The spurious reticulate clause was deleted from the Pillar 4 fine-tuning gate, so the API no longer requires a package it never uses.

findings.title: No CI leg has ever executed the torch code paths: 74 test blocks / 223 expectations / ~3,140 LOC unexercised
findings.correction: Structural claims CONFIRMED exactly: 460 test_that blocks, 184 gated (40.0%), 74 torch-gated, 20 qiskit-gated (test-quantum-vqe.R:5-13, test-quantum-v09.R:11-33), 3143 LOC across the 9 torch-only files (exact), TORCH_INSTALL: 0 for all 5 matrix legs, test-coverage.yaml sets no TORCH_INSTALL and there is no .covrignore / codecov.yml. Counts that are wrong: the suite has 1089 expect_ calls (the figure in the audit brief), not 1209, and 197 of them sit in torch-gated blocks, not 223; 20 R/ files reference torch totalling 6275 LOC, not 18 files / 5904 LOC.
