findings.title: Two competing release checklists contradict each other and describe a deploy action the pkgdown workflow does not use; referenced artefacts do not exist
findings.correction: none — the strongest sub-claim checks out: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:86-92 recommends Pages Source = "GitHub Actions ... uses the pkgdown workflow's deployment artefact directly" and cites "the existing peaceiris/actions-gh-pages step in .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml", but `grep -rn peaceiris .github/` returns nothing and pkgdown.yaml:59-65 deploys via JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0 pushing `docs` to branch `gh-pages`, with no upload-pages-artifact/deploy-pages step — so following the "recommended" option yields a permanently empty site. RELEASE.md:63-67 gives the opposite (correct) instruction. RELEASE.md's "at most 24 MB of installed package" vs cran-comments.md:96 "the *hard* limit is 100 MB" confirmed. .gitignore:64-65 and .Rbuildignore:19/:24 confirmed, including that :24 hard-pins the v3.10.0 filename so a v3.11.0 checklist would ship. Duplicate of "Two competing release checklists, one stale, pointing at a tarball path that does not exist".
findings.evidence: Both checklists survive and still contradict each other. RELEASE.md:1 is headed edaphos - public-release checklist (v2.9.1) and :3 claims four remaining manual actions; RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:1 is a second checklist for a different version, :3 asserts code 100 % ready, CI green, :15 points at /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz which does not exist, and :91-92 names peaceiris/actions-gh-pages while .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:61 uses JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0. The only change either file absorbed in the whole campaign was one title string in an R snippet.
findings.impact: Following the newer, more confident checklist breaks the docs site (choosing Pages Source = GitHub Actions against a branch-push deploy yields a permanently empty site), and both checklists point at build outputs that were deleted, so the "already built" tarball and Zenodo bundle must be regenerated with no recorded provenance. Because the two files disagree, there is no single authoritative release procedure -- and the release procedure is the one process this project has not yet executed even once.
findings.action: Delete RELEASE.md (or reduce it to a pointer) and keep one un-versioned `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`, then generalise .Rbuildignore:24 to `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST.*\.md$`. Correct RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:86-92 to the single working option (branch `gh-pages`, folder `/`) and fix the peaceiris/JamesIves reference at :91-92. Drop the invented "24 MB" and "100 MB" CRAN figures from RELEASE.md:95 and cran-comments.md:96 in favour of the actual 5 MB soft target the note is arguing against. Make artefact generation a step in the checklist rather than a claim that it already happened.
findings.resolution: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md was deleted and RELEASE.md is the single checklist. The deleted file pointed at /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz, which does not exist, and named peaceiris/actions-gh-pages where .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml:61 uses JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0. RELEASE.md carries no version in its title, since both predecessors did and both went stale when the version moved, and its claim that everything besides the four manual steps 'is already in place' is replaced by a pointer to STATUS.md.

findings.title: 33 of 43 NEWS.md releases have no git tag and there is no release-automation workflow, contradicting CONTRIBUTING's tagging promise
findings.correction: The count is 32, not 33: NEWS.md has 43 `^# edaphos` sections and 11 of them are tagged (0.8.0, 0.9.0, 1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.3.1, 1.4.0, 1.5.0, 1.6.0, 3.10.0), leaving 32 untagged (1.7.0 ... 3.9.0). Everything else confirmed exactly: 18 tags with the v1.6.0 -> v3.10.0 jump, CONTRIBUTING.md:87 "Every release gets a git tag (`vX.Y.Z`) and a NEWS.md entry.", 3 workflows only, pkgdown.yaml:14-15 the sole release trigger.
findings.evidence: The NEWS half is moot - ac7b9c2 collapsed NEWS.md to a single heading (line 1, edaphos 0.9.0 development version - not yet released) - but the release-automation half is untouched and the tag ledger is now misleading in a new way. ls .github/workflows/ is still exactly R-CMD-check.yaml, pkgdown.yaml, test-coverage.yaml, with no tag or release job; CONTRIBUTING.md:87 still promises that every release gets a git tag (vX.Y.Z) and a NEWS.md entry. git tag -l returns 19 tags: v0.1.0 to v1.6.0, then v3.10.0 and v4.0.0, neither of which has a NEWS section. STATUS.md's NEWS-versions-with-no-tag metric reads 0 only because tools/status/facts.R:145-152 string-matches NEWS heading 0.9.0 against tag v0.9.0, which points at a394911 (2026-04-22, feat(pillar6): shot-based VQE), an unrelated April commit.
findings.impact: There is no way to reproduce, diff, or archive any release between v1.6.0 and v3.10.0 -- 33 documented releases are unrecoverable as source states. README.md:8 links a `GitHub release` badge and README.md:9 links `/releases/tag/v3.10.0`; the Zenodo-per-release archival model described in README.md:1722-1724 and RELEASE.md:15-53 depends on tags/releases that mostly do not exist. A user reading "v3.5.0 added the RcppArmadillo Gibbs port" (cran-comments.md:119-121) cannot check out that state.
findings.action: Backfill tags where the corresponding commits are identifiable (`git log --oneline --grep='v3\\.' ` on the version-bump commits), or state plainly in CONTRIBUTING.md:82-87 that only milestone versions are tagged. Add a release workflow triggered on `push: tags: ['v*']` that runs R CMD check, builds the tarball, and creates the GitHub release with the matching NEWS.md section as the body -- that also makes pkgdown.yaml:14-15's `release: published` trigger meaningful. Add a CI assertion that DESCRIPTION Version equals the newest `# edaphos` heading in NEWS.md; that single check would have caught the 3.10.0/3.11.0 split.
findings.resolution: .github/workflows/release-tag.yaml provides the release tagging CONTRIBUTING.md:87 promises, manually triggered and defaulting to a dry run. It validates before acting: the tag name must be free, NEWS.md must carry a heading for DESCRIPTION's version, and NEWS must not still mark it a development version. Tested locally, it refuses today on all three counts, which is the point -- the ledger cannot currently accept a release. DESCRIPTION says 0.9.0 while a tag v0.9.0 already exists at a394911 (2026-04-22), 169 commits behind HEAD and minted during the version history NEWS.md withdrew as unreproducible, as were v3.10.0 and v4.0.0. Automating a tag over that would have failed cryptically or invited someone to force-move a published tag, so RELEASE.md states the two honest resolutions -- delete the withdrawn tags, or release under a version the withdrawn history did not consume -- and leaves the choice about published history to the maintainer.

findings.title: Dockerfile is not a reproducibility artefact: builds from GitHub main, unpinned libtorch, R 4.4.1 in no CI leg, v2.1.0 metadata, missing Suggests
findings.correction: Nearly all verified: Dockerfile:66-70 `ARG EDAPHOS_REF=main` + `remotes::install_github(..., dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = 'never')` with no COPY/ADD anywhere, which does render .dockerignore inert; :57-58 unpinned `torch::install_torch(timeout = 600)` against the "byte-reproducible" claim at :41-42; :22 `FROM rocker/geospatial:4.4.1`; stale v2.1.0 at :1, :9, :15, :19, :28 and the RSPM pin `jammy/2026-04-23` described as "the date of the edaphos v2.1.0 release" while DESCRIPTION:3 is 3.10.0; :45-54 installs exactly 38 packages and omits spBayes, ecmwfr, geobr with reticulate commented at :62, against the header claim at :5-6; :72-76 pre-fetches moco-v1. cran-comments.md:15 does list Docker as a test environment. ONE CLAIM IS WRONG: "R 4.4.1 … appears in no leg of the R-CMD-check matrix (release / devel / oldrel-1)" — oldrel-1 resolves dynamically and currently lands on R 4.4.x, so 4.4 is in fact covered; the honest complaint is that the pin is arbitrary and unaligned, not absent. Severity deflated: nothing here affects the package, the tarball, or any user who does not run `docker build`.
findings.evidence: The Dockerfile has never been modified: git log --oneline -- Dockerfile returns exactly one commit, 45e24d2 (feat(v2.1.0)). Every cited line is verbatim at its original number: :1 self-labels v2.1.0, :9 the build tag, :66-70 ARG EDAPHOS_REF=main plus the remotes install of that ref, and the R 4.4.1 base image that appears in no CI matrix leg (.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:23-33 runs release, devel and oldrel-1).
findings.impact: cran-comments.md:15 lists "Docker (Rocker/geospatial): see Dockerfile in repo root" as a test environment, but the image tests whatever is on GitHub main at build time with an unpinned libtorch on an R version nothing else in the project uses -- so it validates nothing about the tarball being submitted. A reviewer (rOpenSci, per RELEASE.md:108) following the documented `docker build` gets an image tagged 2.1.0 containing 3.10.0-or-later code, missing four Suggests, with no rendered vignettes and MoCo v1 weights.
findings.action: Switch to `COPY . /src` + `R -e 'remotes::install_local("/src", dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)'` so the image is built from the tree that `.dockerignore` describes. Pin libtorch by setting `TORCH_HOME`/version env or by installing a fixed torch release. Bump the base to the R version in the CI `release` leg and sync all `2.1.0` strings (Dockerfile:1, 9, 15, 19, 28) to the DESCRIPTION Version, ideally via `ARG EDAPHOS_VERSION`. Add spBayes/ecmwfr/geobr/reticulate to line 45-54 or correct the claim at Dockerfile:5-6. Update the pre-downloaded encoder to the v2 identifier. Add a `docker build` job to CI (it can be `workflow_dispatch`-only) so this file stops rotting.
findings.resolution: The Dockerfile no longer claims a reproducibility it did not deliver. EDAPHOS_REF accepts a commit SHA or tag for a reproducible image and the OCI revision label records whichever was used; the default stays `main` because no tag exists for the current version, and the header says plainly that leaving it there makes a convenience image rather than a reproducibility artefact. Three further defects were fixed: ARG EDAPHOS_REF was declared after the LABEL interpolating it, so every image carried an empty revision; the CRAN snapshot URL hard-coded the `jammy` codename, which on any other base serves no binaries and silently compiles from source, and is now derived from /etc/os-release; and the encoder download was wrapped in try(), so a failed fetch produced an image that builds cleanly, claims offline demos work and has no weights. The base moved from 4.4.1, which matched no CI leg, to 4.6.1, which matches CI's release legs and the committed check.log. NOT VERIFIED BY A BUILD: the Docker daemon was unavailable, so only the structure was checked (instruction order, ARGs declared before use).

findings.title: CI builds vignettes, but 3 of 14 self-truncate to a one-line stub without libtorch -- and CONTRIBUTING tells contributors to skip vignette building entirely
findings.correction: The asymmetry is real: R-CMD-check.yaml:56 `build_args: 'c("--no-manual","--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf")'` omits --no-build-vignettes, while CONTRIBUTING.md:44-45, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:23 and cran-comments.md:4-8/:24-26 all use the weaker `--no-build-vignettes` gate, and a `knit_exit()` is a successful knit that CI cannot detect. But the count is wrong: only TWO vignettes stub out on missing libtorch — vignettes/pilar3-4d-soc.Rmd:85-91 and vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:67-74. vignettes/pilar2-piml-profile.Rmd does NOT: :76-79 sets `.torch_ok` and uses it as a per-chunk `eval=` flag at :191, :202, :228 and :297 — the graceful degradation pattern — and its only `knit_exit` (:80) is on `aqp`. The other cited truncations (dagitty at pilar1-causal.Rmd:61, igraph :171, sp at pilar5-active-learning.Rmd:108, aqp) also do not fire on CI, because r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies installs Suggests; libtorch is the only missing piece. articles/pilar3-4d-real.Rmd is not in the tarball (.Rbuildignore:21).
findings.evidence: Reproduces, with the register's own correction (two vignettes, not three) standing and line numbers moved. vignettes/pilar3-4d-soc.Rmd:91-104 is still a setup gate that calls knitr::knit_exit() when libtorch is absent, and vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd carries the same pattern. CONTRIBUTING still tells contributors to build without vignettes, so no local run exercises the gate.
findings.impact: The tarball CI produces -- and the vignettes CRAN would ship and pkgdown would publish -- contain three stub articles that read "torch runtime (libtorch) not available — skipping vignette" instead of the Pilar 2/3/4 methods papers the README advertises. Nothing in CI detects this, because a `knit_exit()` is a successful knit. Separately, the documented local gate is strictly weaker than the CI gate, so a contributor can satisfy every PR-template checkbox and still push a red build; the maintainer's own 0/0/0 claims were produced under the weaker gate.
findings.action: Add a post-build assertion step to R-CMD-check.yaml that greps the rendered `inst/doc/*.html` for the knit_exit sentinel strings and fails if any vignette is a stub, or gate that assertion to the new libtorch leg from finding 1. Align CONTRIBUTING.md:44-45 and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:23 with the actual CI invocation (drop `--no-build-vignettes`, or state explicitly that CI is stricter). Update cran-comments.md:24-26 to state which vignettes are stubs and why.
findings.resolution: The knitr::knit_exit() gates are kept -- they are correct, and the alternative is a vignette that errors -- but their messages were 'skipping vignette', which is accurate and useless. Each of the six now names the missing dependency, states that what follows is missing rather than empty, and gives the exact command to obtain it (install.packages(...) or torch::install_torch()). All five affected vignettes verified to still render. CONTRIBUTING.md's build advice is also corrected: it told contributors to check with --no-build-vignettes and expect '0/0/0', when the real result is 2 NOTEs and never building vignettes locally is exactly how four articles under articles/ rotted broken unnoticed. It now distinguishes the fast iteration loop from a full build before a PR.

findings.title: Distribution metadata is 9 minor versions stale: CITATION.cff says 2.1.0, README says 2.8.0, .zenodo.json has no version at all
findings.evidence: DESCRIPTION:3 `Version: 3.10.0`. CITATION.cff:109-110 `version: "2.1.0"` / `date-released: "2026-04-23"` -- the same date the Dockerfile:43 RSPM snapshot calls "the date of the edaphos v2.1.0 release". README.md's citation block gives "(Version 2.8.0)" in the prose citation and `version = {2.8.0}` in the BibTeX entry. `.zenodo.json` (6,205 bytes) contains no `version` key at all (`grep -n 'version' .zenodo.json` -> no match). There is no `inst/CITATION` (`ls inst/CITATION` -> no such file), so `citation("edaphos")` falls back to the DESCRIPTION-derived default -- which README describes as "An auto-generated citation is also available in R". README.md's roadmap table still lists `v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝` as pending even though the package is at 3.10.0. No workflow validates or syncs any of these (only 3 workflows exist).
findings.impact: CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json are the files GitHub's "Cite this repository" widget and Zenodo's GitHub integration read. Anyone citing edaphos today from the repo UI cites version 2.1.0 released 2026-04-23; anyone copying the README BibTeX cites 2.8.0; the actual code is 3.10.0 (or 3.11.0 per HEAD~1). A Zenodo deposition driven by `.zenodo.json` would carry no version field, so the concept DOI cannot distinguish releases -- exactly the problem RELEASE.md:15-18 sets out to solve.
findings.action: Update CITATION.cff:109-110 and the README citation block to the DESCRIPTION Version, add a `"version"` key to .zenodo.json, and add a CI step (or a `usethis`-style helper in the release checklist) that asserts DESCRIPTION Version == CITATION.cff version == .zenodo.json version == newest NEWS.md heading. Add a `cff-validator` action so a malformed CITATION.cff is caught. Correct the stale `v3.0.0 CRAN + rOpenSci` roadmap row in README.md.
findings.resolution: Same measurement as F5EF8F6. .zenodo.json carries a version field (it had none) and the README badge reads 4.1.0 rather than 3.10.0; the badge is now generated by patch-readme-metrics.R from DESCRIPTION, and its link points at /releases rather than at a per-tag URL, because the DESCRIPTION version routinely leads the last tag.

findings.title: Chunk option in pilar4-simclr vignette calls `reticulate::` unguarded with broken `&&`/`||` precedence -- hard error in exactly the Docker configuration
findings.evidence: Unchanged in substance; the line moved from :361 to :375. vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:375 is still the chunk header eval=requireNamespace(torch, quietly = TRUE) && reticulate::py_available(), with the unguarded reticulate:: call and the same &&/|| precedence, so it errors rather than skips in exactly the Docker configuration the finding names.
findings.impact: The single environment where the torch vignettes are supposed to render fully -- the Docker image -- is the one environment where this line hard-errors: torch present, reticulate absent. So `docker build` followed by a vignette rebuild cannot reproduce the Pilar 4 article. The same combination can occur on a CRAN check machine that installs torch but not reticulate, producing a vignette-build ERROR rather than a graceful skip, and falsifying the cran-comments.md:49-52 claim.
findings.action: Replace the chunk option at vignettes/pilar4-simclr-embeddings.Rmd:361 with `eval=.torch_ok` (semantically identical, no reticulate dependency), or if the Python path is genuinely intended write `eval=.torch_ok && requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) && reticulate::py_available()`. Add `reticulate` to the Dockerfile install list, or leave it out and confirm the vignette renders. Add a grep-based lint (or an explicit item in the release checklist) for `[a-zA-Z]+::` appearing in a chunk option without a preceding `requireNamespace` in the same expression.

findings.title: cran-comments.md test-suite and install-size figures are contradicted by the tree they describe
findings.correction: none — every number checks out: 460 test_that / 1089 expect_ measured; the single Ollama-shaped skip claim verified (only tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46 `skip_on_cran()` matches `skip_on_cran|skip_if_offline|skip_on_ci` across all of tests/testthat/); benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds = 1,959,632 B = 1,913.70 KB vs the claimed 0.7 MB; benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds = 4,640,252 B = 4,531.50 KB, matching its claimed 4.5 MB; causal_cerrado_real.rds = 63,521 B = 62.03 KB vs the claimed 1.6 MB; the three omitted files are case_cerrado_results.rds 1,434.75 KB, capstone_native_calibration.rds 741.16 KB, capstone_campaign_results.rds 543.31 KB; `du -sh inst/extdata` = 9.6 MB. The tree contains 460 `test_that` blocks / 1089 `expect_` calls across 69 files, and the live run yields 1022 passing expectations, **109** skips (74 torch, 22 dagitty, 9 bnlearn, 3 dbarts, 1 other), 2 errors and 2 warnings -- the warnings are "NAs produced" from `bhs_fit` at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61 (Pilar **7**, not Pilar 8, and not sweep-recycling). Only one test in the whole suite is Ollama/network-shaped (`grep -rn 'skip_on_cran\|skip_if_offline\|skip_on_ci' tests/testthat/` returns exactly one hit, tests/testthat/test-quantum-kernel-rcpp.R:46 `skip_on_cran()`), so the "2 skips ... live Ollama" explanation cannot be right. Install-size figures at cran-comments.md:70-79 are also wrong: it claims extdata is "~8 MB" with `benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.rds 0.7 MB` (actual 1,913.70 KB), `benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds 4.5 MB` (actual 4,531.50 KB, correct) and `causal_cerrado_real.rds 1.6 MB` (actual 62.03 KB), and omits the three next-largest files entirely: `case_cerrado_results.rds` 1,434.75 KB, `capstone_native_calibration.rds` 741.16 KB, `capstone_campaign_results.rds` 543.31 KB. `du -sh inst/extdata` = 9.6 MB.
findings.impact: cran-comments.md is the document a CRAN volunteer reads alongside the tarball. Its headline test figure is off by a factor and its skip explanation is wrong, which invites the exact question it was written to pre-empt ("why are 109 tests skipped?"). Its install-size justification -- the section arguing for an exception to the 5 MB soft cap -- misstates two of the four file sizes it enumerates and omits 2.7 MB of the payload, so the argument does not add up against the directory it describes. This is the kind of arithmetic reviewers check.
findings.action: Regenerate cran-comments.md:28-35 from an actual `devtools::test()` run, reporting test_that blocks vs expectations vs skips separately and grouping the 109 skips by the optional dependency that causes them (that framing also supports the Suggests table at :54-65). Regenerate :70-79 from `ls -l inst/extdata/`, listing every file over 500 KB. Since these numbers must be re-derived every release, add the two commands to the release checklist rather than hand-editing prose.
findings.resolution: cran-comments.md was replaced wholesale by a generated document rendered from a real check log by tools/status/render-cran-comments.R, so the hand-written test-suite and install-size figures the finding indicts no longer exist.

findings.title: No CI leg ever installs libtorch: 25% of R/ and 70 of 460 test blocks are unreachable in all three workflows
findings.correction: Facts confirmed: .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:35 `TORCH_INSTALL: 0`; `grep -rn install_torch` over the repo hits only Dockerfile:58, README.md:343 and R/piml_neural_ode.R:13 — nothing in .github/; test-coverage.yaml and pkgdown.yaml set no torch env at all; total `test_that` blocks = 460; helper-torch.R:7-12 plus the 12 local redefinitions double-gate on the Lantern probe so the blocks skip regardless. Downgraded from blocker because this is a disclosed, deliberate trade-off rather than an oversight — R-CMD-check.yaml:32-34 carries the rationale inline ("Skip torch runtime download on CI ... CI still exercises ~70 % of the test suite"), the code degrades gracefully (all guards are requireNamespace-wrapped), and Dockerfile:57-58 does provide a libtorch environment. It is a real verification gap for six pillars' torch backends, not a broken build.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:32-35 sets `TORCH_INSTALL: 0` with the comment "Skip torch runtime download on CI ... CI still exercises ~70 % of the test suite". `test-coverage.yaml` and `pkgdown.yaml` never install libtorch either (no TORCH_INSTALL, no `torch::install_torch()` step anywhere: grep for `install_torch` matches only Dockerfile:58). Every torch test is double-gated by a runtime probe, so it skips regardless of whether the R `torch` package installs: tests/testthat/helper-torch.R:7-12 (`.skip_if_no_torch()` -> `if (!isTRUE(torch::torch_is_installed())) skip("Lantern (libtorch) backend is not installed.")`), plus locally redefined equivalents at tests/testthat/test-foundation.R:1-4, test-temporal.R:1-4, test-piml-neural.R:1-4, test-foundation-moco.R:1-5, test-piml-hierarchical.R:1-4, test-foundation-tiles.R:2-6, test-foundation-weights.R:3-8. Count of gated blocks: 70 (test-foundation-moco.R 9, test-foundation-finetune.R 8, test-temporal.R 7, test-foundation-posterior.R 5, test-foundation-embed-coords.R 4, test-pilar10-torch.R 4, test-temporal-posterior.R 4, + 12 more files) out of 460 total `test_that` blocks. Torch-backed source LOC: `wc -l` gives 4,990 across R/foundation_moco.R (776), R/foundation_finetune.R (646), R/foundation_tiles.R (416), R/foundation_embed_coords.R (372), R/temporal_convlstm.R (356), R/foundation_weights.R (344), R/temporal_posterior.R (272), R/pilar9_diffusion_torch.R (265), R/piml_hierarchical.R (263), R/foundation_posterior.R (242), R/piml_neural_ode.R (224), R/foundation_simclr.R (216), R/pilar8_neural_operators_torch.R (216), R/piml_neural_ode_ensemble.R (201), R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R (181) = 25.3% of the 19,700 LOC in R/.
findings.impact: Six of the ten advertised pillars (2 Physics-Informed ML, 3 4D Pedometry, 4 Foundation Models, 8 Neural Operators, 9 Diffusion, 10 GAT) have their torch backends verified only on the maintainer's laptop. A green R-CMD-check badge on README.md:5 certifies nothing about them across macOS/Windows/Linux or R devel/oldrel. The recent MPS/CUDA device-placement fix (HEAD, 272b378 "fix(moco): resume on MPS / CUDA") is precisely the class of bug CI exists to catch and precisely the class CI cannot see. Any torch-API break in an upstream release lands silently.
findings.action: Add a sixth matrix leg (ubuntu-latest, R release) that sets `TORCH_INSTALL: 1` and runs `Rscript -e 'torch::install_torch()'` after setup-r-dependencies, with a cache keyed on the torch version (~/.cache/torch or the libtorch install dir). Mark it `continue-on-error: false` but exclude it from the required-checks set initially so a flaky 1 GB download does not block PRs. As a cheap intermediate step, add a `torch-smoke` job that installs libtorch and runs only the 20 torch test files via `testthat::test_dir(filter = ...)`.
findings.resolution: A libtorch CI leg now exists. Commit d51b0d6 added a sixth matrix leg with a libtorch cache and a post-check step that fails the leg if any torch test skipped, so the torch code paths are executed by CI rather than asserted.

findings.title: Pillars 8/9/10 default backend="r" never trains the architecture it is named after, while DESCRIPTION/README mark them "implemented"
findings.correction: The code claims are confirmed and in one place worse than stated. R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:245-258 updates only `W_out` (`W_out <- W_out - lr * grad_W_out`) — so its own comment at :230-235 ("we only update W_in, W_out, b_out") overstates what happens: `W_in` and `b_out` are never touched. R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:242-246 updates only `net$W3`/`net$b3`. R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:249 calls `forward_embed()` once before the loop and :260-270 updates only `W_head`/`b_head`; `a_list` (the GAT attention parameters) is never updated anywhere. But the disclosure claim is REFUTED: "the honest label appears only in one of the three @param texts" is false — all three carry it (pilar8:93 "pure-R ELM-style", pilar9:158 "ELM-style MLP denoiser", pilar10:180 "ELM-style"), so every user-facing Rd page for no_fno_fit/dm_fit/gnn_fit says so, and it is also in the file header R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:26, README.md:235 and NEWS.md:857/:937/:974. The genuinely unlabelled one is `no_deeponet_fit` (pilar8:391, "`"r"` (default)" with no qualifier). Remaining real gaps: DESCRIPTION:21-25 and the README ✅ pillar table make unqualified architecture claims, "ELM-style" is jargon that does not convey "the spectral/attention layers are never trained", and pilar8's code contradicts its own comment.
findings.evidence: Narrowed but still reproduces for Pillars 8 and 9. Pillar 10 is fixed: 51bb2a7 moved forward_all()/backward_all() inside the epoch loop in R/pilar10_graph_nn.R, so the pure-R GAT now trains its own weights, and c416df6 made the backend choice disclosed. The pure-R paths of Pillars 8 and 9 still train a readout only, while DESCRIPTION and README continue to mark both implemented. Note for the register: the Pillar 10 documentation is now stale in the opposite direction - R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:470 and :24-27 still call the fit ELM-style and promise a torch-autograd port scheduled for v2.6.1, while :686-753 runs full analytic reverse-mode backprop.
findings.impact: A reader installing edaphos and calling `no_fno_fit()`, `dm_fit()` or `gnn_fit()` with defaults gets a random-feature ELM with a trained linear readout, not an FNO / DDPM / GAT. Any vignette figure, benchmark table or paper claim produced on the default backend is a claim about random projections, not about the cited architectures (Ho et al. 2020, Velickovic et al. 2018, Li et al. 2021). Since torch is only in Suggests (DESCRIPTION:76) and is not installed on CRAN check machines or in this repo's local environment, the default path is the ONLY path most users and reviewers will ever execute. This is the single highest reputational risk in the package.
findings.action: Either (a) rename the pure-R paths to what they are — `backend = "elm"` / `"random-features"` — and state in DESCRIPTION, README.md:375-381 and R/pillars_roadmap.R that pillars 8/9/10 require torch for the full architecture; or (b) implement backprop for the frozen layers. Option (a) is hours of edits and is honest; option (b) is weeks. Do NOT submit to CRAN/rOpenSci with the current wording. At minimum, add a `message()` at R/pilar8_neural_operators.R:106, R/pilar9_diffusion_models.R:171 and R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:193 when `backend == "r"` naming the limitation.
findings.resolution: README.md's roadmap rows for Pillars 8 and 9 no longer claim what the code denies. The v2.4.0 row said the FNO and DeepONet are implemented 'in pure R ... without torch'; both functions already told users at call time that backend = 'r' is a frozen-spectral or frozen-branch/trunk random-feature reference that does NOT learn the operator, and the row now says the same. The v2.5.0 row carries dm_fit()'s own disclosure that the R sampler is over-dispersed and spatially incoherent. Separately, Pillar 10's documentation was stale in the opposite direction -- the header comment and @param backend still described the ELM-style behaviour that 51bb2a7 removed by moving .gat_forward_all()/.gat_backward_all() inside the epoch loop (verified at R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:688-731), so the pure-R GAT trains every layer. Corrected, with a note that documentation ages in both directions.

findings.title: Off-by-one in the RcppArmadillo BHS backend biases w_post_mean, silently corrupting every predict.edaphos_bhs() for backend="rcpp"
findings.evidence:
R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:276 `for (iter in seq_len(nmcmc))` — iter is 1-based; :314 `if (iter > burn) w_mean <- w_mean + w_cur / (nmcmc - burn)` accumulates exactly (nmcmc - burn) terms over a divisor of (nmcmc - burn). Correct.
src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:103 `for (int iter = 0; iter < nmcmc; ++iter)` — iter is 0-based; :132-133 `if (iter > burn) { w_mean += w_cur / static_cast<double>(nmcmc - burn); }` accumulates only (nmcmc - burn - 1) terms over the same divisor, and drops the draw at 0-based index `burn`.
Proof the intended convention is `>=`: the thinning loop 7 lines below, src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:139 `for (int it = burn; it < nmcmc; it += thin)`, correctly STARTS at 0-based `burn` to mirror R's 1-based `seq(burn + 1L, nmcmc, by = thin)` (R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:318). So the same function uses two different post-burn conventions 7 lines apart.
The corrupted value is load-bearing: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:389-391 `w_new_mean <- as.numeric(t(R_cross) %*% R_tr_inv %*% object$w_post_mean)` feeds the mean of every kriging draw at :394.
No test detects it: tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:37-56 ("backend = 'rcpp' vs 'gibbs': same posterior MEANS within 0.2") compares only `mean(fit$beta_draws[, "x"])`. `w_post_mean` is never compared across backends anywhere in tests/.
findings.impact: Silent numerical divergence between two backends the code and comments claim are equivalent. src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:14-15 asserts "the posterior chain is statistically equivalent up to RNG-draw order" and R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272 claims the marginals are "bit-for-bit identical ... see tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-fastpath.R" — both false for w_post_mean, and unverified by any test.
findings.action: Change src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:132 from `if (iter > burn)` to `if (iter >= burn)`. Then add a test to tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R asserting `expect_equal(fit_r$w_post_mean, fit_cpp$w_post_mean, tolerance = <MCMC noise>)` and a direct assertion that the accumulation count equals `nmcmc - burn` (e.g. run with nmcmc=11, burn=10 and check the result equals the single retained w draw). Also soften the false equivalence claims at src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:14-15 and R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:270-272, which contradict tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-rcpp.R:38-40 ("We don't expect bit-equivalence").
findings.resolution: The exact one-character change the finding prescribed was made, so w_post_mean is no longer biased and predict.edaphos_bhs(backend = rcpp) agrees with the R backend.

findings.title: gnn_embed() returns a different column count per backend and its documented @return is wrong for backend="torch"
findings.correction: none — R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:288-289 documents "@return An `(n, hidden * n_heads)` matrix"; the pure-R path honours it (`emb_dim <- hidden * n_heads` at :225, `h <- do.call(cbind, head_outs)` at :243); the torch path does not (R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:87-89 `curr <- if (concat_l) hidden * n_heads else hidden`, with `emb_dim = ncol(emb_mat)` recorded at :178), and tests/testthat/test-pilar10-torch.R:57-69 pins the divergence with `expect_equal(ncol(emb), 4L)` for hidden = 4, n_heads = 4 plus the comment "# hidden only (mean-pool final head)". Both backends share class `edaphos_gnn_gat` and the bare accessor `gnn_embed()` at :291-294. Downgraded one notch: the main downstream consumer (`qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings`, R/bridges_structure_v3.R:196) reduces `emb` to `n_pcs` principal components and so tolerates either width — the concrete harm is a wrong Rd page, not a runtime break.
findings.evidence:
R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:289 roxygen: "@return An `(n, hidden * n_heads)` matrix -- one row per node." The pure-R path honours this: :225 `emb_dim <- hidden * n_heads`, and multi-head outputs are concatenated at :243 `h <- do.call(cbind, head_outs)`.
The torch path does not. tests/testthat/test-pilar10-torch.R:57-69 ("torch GAT handles multi-head concatenation correctly") fits with `hidden = 4L, n_heads = 4L` and asserts `expect_equal(ncol(emb), 4L)` with the comment "# hidden only (mean-pool final head)" — i.e. 4, not hidden * n_heads = 16.
Both paths return objects of the same S3 class `edaphos_gnn_gat` (R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:284, and the torch constructor in R/pilar10_graph_nn_torch.R:111+), and `gnn_embed()` (:291-294) is a bare `object$emb` accessor with no shape normalisation.
Downstream consumer: R/bridges_structure_v3.R:196 `qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings(gnn_fit, y, ...)` reduces `emb` to `n_pcs` principal components used as QUBITS, and R/bridges_structure_v3.R:226 prints `ncol(x$gnn_fit$emb)` as "GAT emb_dim".
findings.impact: Two backends share one S3 class, one accessor and one Rd page while returning incompatible shapes. The Rd page shipped to users is wrong for one of the two backends, and the divergence is documented only in a test comment. Everything downstream of gnn_embed() — two of the six advertised v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges — is backend-sensitive in an undocumented way.
findings.action: Pick one contract. Simplest: make the torch path concatenate the final layer's heads so both return (n, hidden * n_heads), matching R/pilar10_graph_nn.R:289; otherwise change the roxygen @return to document the per-backend shape explicitly and record `emb_dim` in both fit objects. Either way add a test in tests/testthat/test-pilar10-gat.R that fits both backends with the same hidden/n_heads and asserts `ncol(gnn_embed(fit_r)) == ncol(gnn_embed(fit_t))`.
findings.resolution: man/gnn_embed.Rd documents the average_heads argument and the column count each setting produces; the pure-R path in R/pilar10_graph_nn.R implements the same argument, so both backends are described by one \value.

findings.title: Rank-deficient design matrix poisons the entire BHS Gibbs chain to NA on iteration 1, then hard-errors — and the test's own comment about it is wrong
findings.correction: none of substance — the whole propagation chain is verified line by line: R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 unguarded `beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)`; :283 `rhs_w`, :286 `mu_w`, :288 `w_cur`, :302 `rate_s`, :303 first `rgamma`, :306 `resid`, :309 second `rgamma` — matching the two live "NAs produced" warnings; `.chol_jitter` at :246-256 with the unguarded final fallback `chol(M + diag(1e-2 * mean(diag(M)), nrow(M)))` at :255 that throws once `sigma2` is NA at :280. The ordering critique is correct and is the finding's best point: the w-update at :277-288 consumes `beta` before the beta-update at :290-298, so the test's comment at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:66-67 ("NA beta from lm.fit init is OK -- Gibbs will re-sample") is factually false, and the `tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL)` + `expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` at :57-69 passes either way. Minor: the rcpp analogue is src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:91 (`arma::vec beta = arma::solve(X, y);`), not :93, and arma::solve on a rank-deficient X warns/throws rather than yielding NA, so that failure mode differs. Severity deflated: the outcome is two warnings plus a loud error, not silently wrong inference, on a degenerate input.
findings.evidence:
R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238 `beta <- as.numeric(stats::lm.fit(X, y)$coefficients)` — `lm.fit` returns NA for aliased columns of a rank-deficient X and there is no `is.na()` guard.
Propagation, all in the same function: :283 `rhs_w <- (y - as.numeric(X %*% beta)) / tau2` → all-NA because `X %*% c(b0, NA)` is NA; :286 `mu_w` NA; :288 `w_cur` NA; :302 `rate_s <- prior_ig_b + 0.5 * as.numeric(crossprod(w_cur, Rinv %*% w_cur))` NA → :303 `stats::rgamma(1, shape = shape_s, rate = rate_s)` returns NA with warning "NAs produced"; :306 `resid` NA → :309 second `rgamma` → second "NAs produced". That is exactly the 2 warnings observed at tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:61.
Iteration 2 then has `sigma2 = NA`, so :280 `prec_w <- Rinv * (1 / sigma2)` is all-NA, `.chol_jitter` (:246-256) exhausts its 8 jitter retries and its unguarded final fallback `chol(M + diag(1e-2 * mean(diag(M)), nrow(M)))` at :255 throws.
The guarding test is tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69, which wraps the call in `tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL)` and asserts `expect_true(is.null(fit) || inherits(fit, "edaphos_bhs"))` — it passes either way. Its comment at :66-67 states "NA beta from lm.fit init is OK -- Gibbs will re-sample", which is factually wrong: the w-update at :277-288 consumes beta BEFORE the beta-update at :290-298, so the chain is already NA by the time beta would be re-drawn.
The rcpp backend has the analogous unguarded init at src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:93 `arma::vec beta = arma::solve(X, y);`.
findings.impact: A common, benign data condition produces two stray warnings plus a cryptic linear-algebra error from three frames deep, with no indication that the cause was a collinear covariate. This is precisely the class of failure the v3.8.0 `.stopf()`/hint machinery was added to eliminate — and `bhs_fit` is the one function that already uses `.assert_type` (:91-100), so the omission is inconsistent within a single function body.
findings.action: At R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:238, detect rank deficiency and fail loudly: `qrX <- qr(X); if (qrX$rank < ncol(X)) .stopf("design matrix is rank-deficient (rank %d < %d columns).", qrX$rank, ncol(X), hint = "Drop collinear or zero-variance covariates from the formula.")`. As a belt-and-braces fix also add `beta[!is.finite(beta)] <- 0` and mirror the rank check before src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp:93. Then rewrite tests/testthat/test-pilar7-bhs-edge.R:57-69 to assert the specific error with `expect_error(..., regexp = "rank-deficient")` instead of accepting both outcomes, and delete the incorrect comment at :66-67.
findings.resolution: Same measurement as FD825FD: the rank-deficient design is rejected before the Gibbs loop starts, so neither of the two "NAs produced" warnings is emitted.

findings.title: Twelve copies of skip_if_no_torch() in three divergent flavours, orphaning the helper-torch.R that was added to replace them
findings.correction: none on the counts — I reproduced them exactly: helper-torch.R:7 defines `.skip_if_no_torch()` with the header rationale at :1-6, used at 18 call sites across 7 files; 12 test files define a local undotted `skip_if_no_torch()` (test-foundation.R:1, test-piml-neural.R:1, test-piml-hierarchical.R:1, test-temporal.R:1, test-foundation-moco.R:1, test-foundation-tiles.R:2, test-piml-posterior.R:3, test-temporal-posterior.R:3, test-foundation-posterior.R:3, test-piml-neural-ode-ensemble.R:3, test-foundation-weights.R:3, test-foundation-finetune.R:7), used at 52 sites. The link to live ERROR 2 is right: test-foundation-weights.R:29-36 sits two lines below its own unused local gate. TWO OVERSTATEMENTS: it is really 2 behaviours, not 3 — variants (a) and (c) are functionally identical, since `isTRUE()` is pure defensiveness around a function that returns a logical and the claimed "NA return would error rather than skip" is speculative; and the deeper fix for ERROR 2 is arguably to validate `n_channels` before `.moco_require_torch()` at R/foundation_weights.R:294, not to add a skip.
findings.evidence: Reproduces and is worse than reported. tests/testthat/helper-torch.R:7 still defines the canonical dotted .skip_if_no_torch(), used at 19 call sites in 7 files, while 13 test files each define their own non-dotted skip_if_no_torch() that shadows it: test-foundation.R, test-foundation-finetune.R, test-foundation-moco.R, test-foundation-posterior.R, test-foundation-tiles.R, test-foundation-weights.R, test-piml-hierarchical.R, test-piml-hierarchical-guards.R, test-piml-neural.R, test-piml-neural-ode-ensemble.R, test-piml-posterior.R, test-temporal.R, test-temporal-posterior.R. That is 13 copies in 4 flavours, up from 12 in 3.
findings.impact: 70 gate call sites, 13 definitions, 3 behaviours. Variant (b) actually allocates a tensor, which is the only one that reliably detects a broken-but-present Lantern; variant (c) trusts a flag. The centralisation effort that produced helper-torch.R stalled after 7 of 19 files, and the un-migrated files are precisely where the pillar-4 work lives. This is also the mechanism behind the live ERROR 2: tests/testthat/test-foundation-weights.R:28-37 sits two lines below a local gate definition it simply forgot to call.
findings.action: Delete all 12 local definitions and rename the 52 undotted call sites to `.skip_if_no_torch()`. Adopt variant (b)'s tensor allocation inside helper-torch.R:7 (it is the only sound check) while keeping the `isTRUE()` wrapper. Then grep-assert in CI that `skip_if_no_torch <- function` appears nowhere under tests/ so the duplication cannot come back.
findings.resolution: The thirteen local definitions of skip_if_no_torch() are gone; tests/testthat/helper-torch.R holds one definition plus a non-dotted alias so the existing call sites resolve to it. The three flavours were not equivalent -- some checked torch_is_installed(), some wrapped it in tryCatch, some allocated a real tensor -- and the consolidation adopted the strongest, because torch_is_installed() reports the runtime is present rather than working, and a partial or architecture-mismatched Lantern answers TRUE and then dies on the first tensor. Deduplicating onto the shortest variant would have weakened thirteen files at once. Skip count verified unchanged at 15.

findings.title: al_fit(num.trees=) has no lower bound against ranger's undocumented OOB-quantile minimum, and the test that breaks is unseeded — a ~25% flaky ERROR
findings.correction: Third restatement of the same defect, and its headline number is fabricated. Code facts verified (R/active_fit.R:1-10 hardcoding quantreg/keep.inbag; :52-53 and R/active_loop.R:73 accepting any num.trees; roxygen :29; the ranger 0.18.0 `minoob < 10` stop confirmed by deparse; tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 with bare `stats::rnorm(40L)` and 50L). But "~25% flaky" is asserted with no measurement anywhere in the evidence and is wrong on both counts: the unconditional across-seeds rate is 12.0% (I measured 24/200 at the exact shape), and within the suite the rate is 100% because line 7 of the same file calls set.seed(1L) — I reproduced the failure 3/3 by replaying that stream. "The suite is non-deterministically red" is therefore false; it is deterministically red on ranger 0.18.0. Duplicate of findings 12 and 20; findings 12 and 20 at least quote a measured number.
findings.evidence:
R/active_fit.R:1-10 `.fit_core()` hardcodes `quantreg = TRUE, keep.inbag = TRUE` in the `ranger::ranger()` call. R/active_fit.R:52-53 `al_fit(..., num.trees = 500L, ...)` and R/active_loop.R:73 `al_loop(..., num.trees = 500L, ...)` accept any value with no validation; the roxygen at R/active_fit.R:29 says only "Integer, number of trees (default 500)".
ranger 0.18.0's quantreg branch (verified by deparsing `ranger::ranger` in the installed 0.18.0) ends with: `minoob <- min(rowSums(inbag.counts == 0)); if (minoob < 10) { stop("Error: Too few trees for out-of-bag quantile regression.") }` — i.e. EVERY observation must be out-of-bag in at least 10 trees.
tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30-35 has no `set.seed()` anywhere in the block; it builds `df` from bare `stats::rnorm(40L)` and calls `al_fit(df, target = "y", covariates = "x", num.trees = 50L)`.
findings.impact: The suite is non-deterministically red, which destroys the credibility of NEWS.md v3.10.0's "1 345 tests pass / 0 errors". Independently, any user who reduces `num.trees` for speed on a small pilot dataset — the exact use case active learning targets — gets a cryptic ranger error with no hint, from a function whose documented parameter contract has no lower bound. All other al_* tests use 100-200 (P(failure) negligible), so 50 is the single unlucky value in the suite.
findings.action: Two changes. (1) In R/active_fit.R, before the ranger call at :3, add `if (num.trees < 100L) .stopf("`num.trees` = %d is too small for out-of-bag quantile regression.", num.trees, hint = "ranger requires every observation to be out-of-bag in >= 10 trees; use num.trees >= 100.")` and document the floor at :29 and R/active_loop.R:36. (2) Add `set.seed(3L)` at the top of tests/testthat/test-active-quantum-posterior.R:30 and raise `num.trees` there to 100L — every other al_* test already uses >= 100.
findings.resolution: Both prescribed changes landed: a derived lower bound now exists for num.trees, and the flaky test was seeded and given a valid tree count.

findings.title: Same loop-invariant matrix product recomputed n_draws times, copy-pasted into two files
findings.evidence:
Site 1 — R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:290-298. `R_tr_inv` is computed at :278 and `R_cross` at :283, both outside the loop. Inside `for (i in idx) {` at :290, line :295 reads `quadratic <- colSums((R_tr_inv %*% R_cross) * R_cross)` — the expression depends on neither `i` nor anything assigned in the loop body (:291-292 only read `sigma2_draws[i]` / `tau2_draws[i]`). Default `n_draws = 200L` (:261).
Site 2 — R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:384-396, the same copy-paste. `R_tr_inv` at :373 and `R_cross` at :379 are loop-invariant; inside `for (i in seq_along(idx)) {` at :385, lines :389-391 read `w_new_mean <- as.numeric(t(R_cross) %*% R_tr_inv %*% object$w_post_mean)` — no dependence on `i`. Default `n_draws = 500L` (:354).
findings.impact: Two of the package's headline v3.0.0 bridge/prediction entry points are two to three orders of magnitude slower than necessary on realistic problem sizes. This is the same defect duplicated by copy-paste, in the same idiom (build R_tr_inv and R_cross, then loop over posterior draws), which is a concrete measurement of how much of the cross-pillar bridge layer is duplicated rather than shared. Note the irony: this sits alongside a 156-line RcppArmadillo port (src/bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp) written to buy a 10-15x speedup on the sampler.
findings.action: Hoist line R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:295 to just after :283, and hoist R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:389-391 to just after :379. Both are one-line moves with no behaviour change (verify with a before/after `expect_equal` on the returned object under a fixed seed). Then extract the shared "exponential-correlation kriging weights from coords" block — duplicated at R/pilar7_bayesian_hierarchical.R:370-379 and R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:275-283 — into one internal helper in R/core_utils.R.
findings.resolution: Both copies of the loop-invariant product were hoisted out of their loops.

findings.title: Naming schism: pilar/pillar, ordinal/domain module names, al_* vs active_*, and five undocumented cryptic export prefixes
findings.evidence: Reproduces on every sub-claim but one. RESOLVED sub-claim: R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 now says ten pillars and its namespace table at :8-19 has ten rows including bhs_*. Still open: the pilar/pillar spelling schism persists across R/ file names and function prefixes, al_* and active_* still coexist as parallel prefixes, and the five cryptic export prefixes are still undocumented.
findings.impact: A contributor cannot infer a file's contents or a function's prefix from any single source of truth: the roadmap covers 6 of 10 pillars, DESCRIPTION claims 10, README documents `al_*` for files named `active_*`, and print methods emit Portuguese while the docs emit English. The function-name shadowing is a live hazard: inside `al_query_bhs`, `al_query_diffusion`, `gnn_causal_discovery` and `qf_krr_on_gat_embeddings` the identifiers `bhs_fit`, `dm_fit` and `gnn_fit` resolve to data, so any future refactor that adds a refit call inside those bodies fails with "attempt to apply non-function".
findings.action: Three mechanical passes, none behaviour-changing. (1) `git mv` the 7 R/pilar*.R files and 17 test files to domain names matching pillars 1-6 (bhs_*.R, neural_operators*.R, diffusion*.R, graph_nn*.R) and fix the two user-facing print strings at R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:313 and R/bridges_structure_v3.R:225 to "Pillar". (2) Extend R/pillars_roadmap.R:8-15 from six rows to ten, retitle :1 from "six pillars" to "ten pillars", and add the `bhs_*`/`no_*`/`dm_*`/`gnn_*`/`qf_*` namespace entries; either rename `active_learning_posterior` to `al_posterior` (with an alias for back-compat) or amend the `al_*` claim in R/pillars_roadmap.R:14 and README.md:379. (3) Rename the four shadowing parameters to `fit` or `object` (R/bridges_active_learning_v3.R:260, :174; R/bridges_structure_v3.R:50, :196) and re-roxygenise. Consider renaming the `no_*` prefix to `fno_*`/`don_*`.

findings.title: Twelve exported functions are never referenced anywhere in tests/, including the entire advertised tile-source pipeline
findings.evidence: Reproduces and is worse. All twelve originally named exports still have zero references anywhere under tests/, including the tile-source pipeline (foundation_tile_source_*), causal_ontology_agrovoc, causal_ontology_envo, edaphos_zenodo_release and foundation_build_cerrado_stack; the count is now 14 untested exports of 178 (was 12 of 169).
findings.impact: The five tile sources plus the Cerrado stack builder are the exact functions a reviewer would run to reproduce the pretrained `edaphos-cerrado-moco-v1` encoder advertised in R/pillars_roadmap.R:13 and README, and none has a single assertion — not even a schema/argument-validation test that could run offline. `edaphos_zenodo_release` (R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:38, 223 lines) performs authenticated HTTP publishing to Zenodo from inside a CRAN package with zero tests. `llm_annotation_launch` (R/llm_annotation.R:665) is likewise untested.
findings.action: Add offline tests for the cheap half first: argument validation and returned-descriptor schema for each `foundation_tile_source_*` (they should be pure constructors — assert the returned list's fields and that a bad CRS/bbox errors) and for `foundation_build_cerrado_stack` with a stubbed source. Gate the network-touching halves behind `skip_on_cran()` + `skip_if_offline()`. Separately, reconsider whether `edaphos_zenodo_release` belongs in R/ at all — it is release tooling, not a soil-mapping algorithm, and shipping it as a public export means CRAN users can POST to Zenodo; moving it to inst/scripts/ removes both the test debt and the API-surface cost.
findings.resolution: Of 178 exports, 12 were referenced by no test and 8 of those had only \dontrun examples, so they executed nowhere at all. Three new offline test files cover them: tests/testthat/test-foundation-tile-sources.R (206 assertions over the five foundation_tile_source_* functions), test-causal-ontology-envo.R (28), test-zenodo-release.R (67). No network, no Shiny launch, no writes outside a tempdir. Verified by defect injection rather than by assertion count: the tile-source file catches all 16 separately injected defects, and breaking the ontology term normalisation and the Zenodo SHA-256 computation fails 3 and 1 assertions respectively. Suite 2215 -> 2518. A side finding surfaced while injecting: the term-normalisation logic is duplicated verbatim between causal_ontology_agrovoc and causal_ontology_envo.

findings.title: `Depends: R (>= 3.5)` is falsified by two features requiring R 4.0.0 and R 3.6.0
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:90-91` declares `Depends: R (>= 3.5)`.

Two hard violations:
1. `tools::R_user_dir()` was introduced in **R 4.0.0**. Used at `R/foundation_weights.R:111` (`root <- cache_dir %||% tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache")`) and `R/foundation_embed_coords.R:226` (`cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache")`). On R 3.5/3.6 the whole pretrained-weights cache path (`foundation_weights_download/load`, `foundation_embed_at_coords`) errors with `object 'R_user_dir' not found`.
2. `NAMESPACE:15` is `S3method(ggplot2::autoplot,edaphos_posterior)` — delayed S3 registration against a generic in a Suggests-only package. That `pkg::generic` form of `S3method()` was added in **R 3.6.0**; on R 3.5.x package load fails outright.

The CI matrix (`.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:23-27`) is macos/windows/ubuntu at `release`, `devel`, `oldrel-1` — with R 4.6.1 current, `oldrel-1` is R 4.5.x, so the declared floor is never exercised anywhere.
findings.impact: CRAN builds against the declared minimum. A user (or a CRAN back-check machine) on R 3.5/3.6 gets a package that either fails to load or errors in all of Pillar 4's weight-loading API — reported to the maintainer as a broken package after acceptance.
findings.action: Change `DESCRIPTION:90-91` to `Depends: R (>= 4.0)`, and add an explicit `r: '4.0'` (or `'oldrel-3'`) leg to `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml` so the declared floor is actually tested.
findings.resolution: DESCRIPTION Depends: R (>= 4.0).

findings.title: 5 of 14 vignettes are written in Portuguese while DESCRIPTION declares `Language: en-US`
findings.correction: The language mismatch is real: DESCRIPTION:31 `Language: en-US`; PT-stopword counts reproduce as capstone-cerrado-campaign 193, pilar1-pilar4-iv 138, causal-discovery-trio 76, llm-annotation-workflow 64, pilar4-pilar6-quantum 44, everything else 0-1; capstone's title AND `%\VignetteIndexEntry{}` are Portuguese; DESCRIPTION:8 "organised" and :27 "synthesised" are en-GB; 22 man/*.Rd carry en-GB forms. Two claims are wrong. (1) "inst/WORDLIST ... nothing consumes it" — CONTRIBUTING.md:47 and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md both mandate `devtools::spell_check()`, which is `spelling::spell_check_package()` and reads inst/WORDLIST as its ignore list; the 2032-line file is the documented dev-workflow artefact, not dead. (2) The stated check mechanism is wrong: `R CMD check --as-cran` does not run aspell over vignettes, and "checking for detritus in the temp directory" has nothing to do with spelling — CRAN's automated spell check covers DESCRIPTION/Rd only. The rOpenSci English-documentation concern stands on its own.
findings.evidence: Reproduces unchanged; only the denominator moved, to 19 vignettes. DESCRIPTION:32 is still Language: en-US, while vignettes/capstone-cerrado-campaign.Rmd and the pilar1/pilar4 Portuguese vignettes still carry hundreds of Portuguese stopwords each (219 in the capstone alone).
findings.impact: CRAN runs `aspell` against the declared `Language`; five Portuguese vignettes plus en-GB spellings in DESCRIPTION produce a large `checking for detritus`/spelling NOTE and a near-certain reviewer request ("the Language field must match the documentation language"). rOpenSci requires English-language documentation outright, so 5 of 14 vignettes are out of policy for the review the checklist is preparing to file.
findings.action: Decide one way: either translate the 5 Portuguese vignettes to English (and fix `organised`->`organized`, `synthesised`->`synthesized` in DESCRIPTION:8,27), or move them out of `vignettes/` into `articles/` and drop them from the tarball. Then add `spelling` to Suggests plus `tests/spelling.R` so `inst/WORDLIST` is actually enforced instead of being 20 KB of shipped dead weight.
findings.resolution: DESCRIPTION declares Language: en-US, pt-BR, which is what the field accepts and what is true: five of the vignettes are written in Portuguese. Counted before deciding -- an initial detector returned zero because its threshold was set too high, which is why the count was measured per file rather than asserted.

findings.title: DESCRIPTION Title/Description violate CRAN style: marketing adjectives, unquoted software names, zero method references
findings.correction: none — DESCRIPTION:2 `Title: Disruptive Algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping`; :8 "Frontier algorithms…"; unquoted software names verified at :16 (SimCLR / MoCo), :19 (ZZFeatureMap), :21 (RcppArmadillo backend), :22 (DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator), :23 (DDPM); `grep -l '\\doi{' man/*.Rd | wc -l` = 0 and `grep -c 'doi:' DESCRIPTION` = 0 while vignettes/references.bib is 31,291 bytes; Authors@R at :4-7 is `role = c("aut", "cre")` with no "cph" against `LICENSE:2 COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Hugo Rodrigues` and `License: MIT + file LICENSE` at :29; :25 "Six v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges" and :26 unquoted `edaphos_posterior`. Note the version-stale prose at :25 is a second six-vs-ten instance inside the very file that says "ten" at :8.
findings.evidence:
`DESCRIPTION:2` — `Title: Disruptive Algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping`. `DESCRIPTION:8` — `Description: Frontier algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping organised around ten research pillars:`. CRAN's checklist explicitly asks maintainers to drop promotional language; "Disruptive" and "Frontier" are exactly that, and the same wording is repeated in `inst/rosc/submission.md:13` and `vignettes/case-cerrado-end-to-end.Rmd:28-30` (which itself calls the claim "falsifiable").

Software/package names are unquoted throughout the Description, where CRAN requires single quotes: `SimCLR / MoCo` (:16), `ZZFeatureMap` (:19), `RcppArmadillo backend` (:21), `DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator` (:22), `DDPM` (:23).

**No references at all.** `grep '\\doi{'` over `man/*.Rd` returns **0 files**, and the Description contains no `<doi:...>` or `<https://...>` citation. Yet the Description names ten published method families (backdoor adjustment, Neural ODE, ConvLSTM, Ensemble Kalman Filter, SimCLR, MoCo, ZZFeatureMap, DeepONet, FNO, DDPM, GAT) whose papers *are* already catalogued in `vignettes/references.bib` (31 KB) and in `\references` blocks (e.g. `man/uncertainty_calibrate.Rd` cites Gneiting & Raftery 2007, `man/quantum_kernel.Rd` cites Havlicek 2019).

`Authors@R` (`:4-7`) gives Hugo Rodrigues roles `c("aut", "cre")` only — no `"cph"` — while `LICENSE:2` declares `COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Hugo Rodrigues` for the `MIT + file LICENSE` at `:29`.

The Description also embeds version-specific prose that goes stale immediately: `:25` "Six v3.0.0 cross-pillar bridges", and `:26` names an internal class (`edaphos_posterior`) unquoted.
findings.impact: "Please add references describing the methods in the Description field in the form authors (year) <doi:...>", "please put software names in single quotes", "please add the copyright holder (cph) role" and "please avoid marketing language" are four of the five most common CRAN first-round replies. Each costs a submission round-trip of days.
findings.action: Rewrite DESCRIPTION:2 to a neutral Title (e.g. `Advanced Algorithms for Digital Soil Mapping`); single-quote every software name in the Description; append 3-5 anchor references pulled from `vignettes/references.bib` as `Author (Year) <doi:10.xxxx/yyyy>`; add `"cph"` to the Authors@R role vector; drop the `v3.0.0`/`edaphos_posterior` internals from the Description.
findings.resolution: DESCRIPTION was rewritten to CRAN style: the marketing adjectives are gone, software names are quoted, and the Title and Description no longer make the claims the finding cites.

findings.title: `src/Makevars.win` documents a Unix `src/Makevars` that does not exist
findings.evidence: Untouched since the audited commit - src/Makevars.win does not appear in git diff --stat 272b378 HEAD. ls src/ is Makevars.win, RcppExports.cpp, bhs_gibbs_rcpp.cpp, quantum_kernel_rcpp.cpp (plus build objects): there is no Unix src/Makevars, yet Makevars.win:1-2 still describes itself as mirroring the Unix Makevars.
findings.impact: On Linux/macOS the LAPACK/BLAS symbols currently resolve only by accident — because the already-loaded R process exports them and `.so` symbol resolution is lazy. On CRAN's Solaris/alternative-BLAS/`--disable-BLAS-shlib` build farms that assumption can break with the same `undefined reference to ddot_` the Windows file was written to fix, on a platform the CI matrix does not cover. The comment also misleads the next maintainer into believing a Unix counterpart exists.
findings.action: Add `src/Makevars` containing `PKG_LIBS = $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS)` (the standard RcppArmadillo skeleton), which makes `Makevars.win`'s comment true and removes the platform-dependent link assumption.
findings.resolution: src/Makevars.win's comment claimed to mirror a Unix src/Makevars that does not exist. It does not need to exist: on Unix, R supplies $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS) to RcppArmadillo packages by default, so an explicit file would restate the default. The comment now says that, and explains why Windows needs the flags spelled out for rtools ld.exe.

findings.title: RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md instructs the maintainer to upload two artefacts that do not exist, and asserts a green state contradicted by the live test run
findings.correction: Confirmed: :13-15 names /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz (`ls` -> No such file or directory); :53-55 and :62 name tools/zenodo_release.zip, absent and .gitignore'd (line 65, plus tools/zenodo_release/ at 64); :3-4 headlines "code 100 % ready, CI green, all artefacts regenerated". One sub-point is a category error: :15's "17 MB" is the source *tarball* while cran-comments.md:69's "~13 MB" is the *installed* size — different quantities, not a contradiction. The version-scope point holds (DESCRIPTION:3 / NEWS.md:1 are 3.10.0 while HEAD~1 is the v3.11.0 hand-off commit and tools/pretrain/V1_3_2_HANDOFF.md exists).
findings.evidence: The file has never been modified; its only commit is 65e8b91. RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:13-15 still instructs the maintainer to submit /tmp/edaphos_release_tarballs/edaphos_3.10.0.tar.gz (17 MB), which does not exist, and :3 still asserts code 100 % ready, CI green. The version reset makes it worse: it announces v3.10.0 as ready to submit in a tree whose DESCRIPTION:3 says 0.9.0 and whose NEWS.md:1 says not yet released.
findings.impact: A maintainer following this checklist step-by-step reaches step 1 or 3 and finds nothing to submit or upload, with no recorded command to regenerate either artefact. The "CI green / 100 % ready" header actively suppresses the two real test failures that should gate the release.
findings.action: Replace the hard-coded artefact paths with the commands that produce them (`devtools::build()`, and whatever script built `zenodo_release.zip` — it is not in `tools/`). Rename/renumber the checklist for the actual next version, add a NEWS.md `# edaphos 3.11.0` section for the HEAD~1 work, and gate the header claim on a passing `devtools::test()`.

findings.title: Two overlapping release checklists disagree with each other and both claim to be the authoritative list of remaining steps
findings.evidence: Reproduces. Both documents exist and both claim authority. RELEASE.md:1 edaphos - public-release checklist (v2.9.1) and :3 This file lists the four remaining manual actions; RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:1 Release checklist for edaphos v3.10.0 and :3-7 its own four steps. Neither references the other, and the package they describe is now versioned 0.9.0 (DESCRIPTION:3).
findings.impact: There is no single answer to "what is left to do before release". A maintainer following RELEASE.md targets v2.9.1 and is told the DOI badge points at v0.2.0; following RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md they are told everything is "code 100 % ready, CI green" (RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:3-4), which finding #4 shows is false. The version-specific .Rbuildignore pattern guarantees a future R CMD check NOTE about a non-standard top-level file.
findings.action: Delete RELEASE.md (its v2.9.1 content is superseded), rename the survivor to a version-free `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`, and change .Rbuildignore:24 to `^RELEASE-CHECKLIST.*\.md$` so it stays excluded across releases. Reconcile the install-size numbers to one figure and fold RELEASE.md:16-18's concept-DOI-resolves-to-v0.2.0 warning into the surviving checklist.
findings.resolution: Same fix as F29E750: the two competing checklists are now one. RELEASE.md no longer claims a version and states that the four manual steps are the third-party half of a release, not the whole of the remaining work.

findings.title: The "ten pillars" identity exists only in the unreleased HEAD; every other metadata artefact still says six
findings.correction: none — `git rev-list --oneline v3.10.0..HEAD` contains 797adc5 "chore(cran-prep): tighten DESCRIPTION (10 pillars instead of 6)", so DESCRIPTION:8-9 "organised around ten research pillars" is indeed post-tag. Every counter-citation verified: CITATION.cff:7 "six research pillars" and :33 "all six pillars"; .zenodo.json:3 six-item `<ol>`; _pkgdown.yml:44 and :66; R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 "Roadmap and status of the six pillars of edaphos" (and its table at :8-19 enumerates only pillars 1-6); README.md:371 "## The six pillars at a glance" plus 11 further "six pillars" hits (12 total). Against them: README.md:10 `pillars-10%2F10%20shipped`, INTRO.md:42 "## The ten research pillars", inst/rosc/submission.md:14 "ten research pillars", CONTRIBUTING.md:60 "Every \"pillar\" (1-10) lives in `R/pilarN_*.R`", and R/pilar7_*.R–R/pilar10_*.R on disk.
findings.evidence: Commit 797adc5 "chore(cran-prep): tighten DESCRIPTION (10 pillars instead of 6)" landed AFTER the v3.10.0 tag (it is in `git rev-list v3.10.0..HEAD`), so DESCRIPTION:8-9 "organised around ten research pillars" is the only ten-pillar statement in released metadata terms -- and it belongs to an unversioned commit. Everything else still says six: CITATION.cff:7 "organised across six research pillars"; .zenodo.json:3 "organised across six research pillars" with an `<ol>` of exactly six items; _pkgdown.yml:44 "Six research pillars"; _pkgdown.yml:66 "Capstone — six pillars integrated"; R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 "#' Roadmap and status of the six pillars of edaphos"; README.md:371 "## The six pillars at a glance" (a table with six pillar rows) plus 12 further "six pillars" occurrences in README.md. Meanwhile README.md:10 badges "pillars-10%2F10%20shipped", INTRO.md:42 says "## The ten research pillars", inst/rosc/submission.md:14 says "ten research pillars", CONTRIBUTING.md:60 says "Every \"pillar\" (1-10) lives in `R/pilarN_*.R`", and R/pilar7_*.R through R/pilar10_*.R exist on disk.
findings.impact: The package's most basic self-description is 6-vs-10 depending on which file you open, and the tie-breaking file (DESCRIPTION) only reached its current wording in a commit that carries no version number -- so there is no released version of edaphos that consistently claims ten pillars. Every downstream metadata consumer (Zenodo via .zenodo.json, GitHub citation widget via CITATION.cff, docs site via _pkgdown.yml, `?edaphos-roadmap` via R/pillars_roadmap.R) will keep publishing "six" after the DESCRIPTION change ships.
findings.action: In one commit, propagate the ten-pillar wording from DESCRIPTION:8-28 to CITATION.cff:4-107, .zenodo.json:3, _pkgdown.yml:43-48 and :66, and R/pillars_roadmap.R:1 (whose roxygen table also needs rows for Pilares 7-10, then re-roxygenise man/edaphos-roadmap.Rd). Update README.md:371 and its anchor consumers (README.md:10, :210). Tie the whole change to the version bump from finding #1 so "ten pillars" first appears in a numbered, tagged release.
findings.resolution: CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json and _pkgdown.yml now say ten research pillars and enumerate all ten; DESCRIPTION, README.md, R/pillars_roadmap.R and R/edaphos-package.R already did. The only surviving "six pillars" strings are historical and correct -- the v1.7.0 capstone integrated the six pillars that existed then. Measured by grepping for the phrase and excluding occurrences qualified by that/then/of-v1.x.

findings.title: The 84 KB README documents nothing after v2.8.0; its only 3.x reference is the version badge
findings.evidence: wc -c README.md = 111304; README.md:9 version badge 0.9.0-dev; README.md:245 heading v2.7.0 - v2.8.0; README.md:2173 the last completed roadmap row, v2.8.0.
findings.impact: The public front page of the project describes a 6-pillar package at v1.7.0/v2.8.0 while the badges beside it claim 3.10.0 and 10/10 pillars. Pillars 7-10 -- Bayesian hierarchical spatial, neural operators, diffusion models, GATs, i.e. R/pilar7_*.R through R/pilar10_*.R and roughly the whole v2.3.0-v3.6.0 arc -- are invisible to anyone reading the README, and the ten-vs-six contradiction is visible within a single screen (badge line 10 vs heading line 371).
findings.action: Either add Pillar 7-10 sections and TOC entries and retitle README.md:371 to "The ten pillars at a glance" (updating the anchor at README.md:10 and the TOC entry at README.md:210), or drop the "10/10 pillars" badge until the README backs it. Delete the stale "🆕" prefixes at README.md:147 and :230, correct README.md:1674-1675 to the real check status (see finding #4), and change "six" to "seven" at README.md:364.

findings.title: .zenodo.json carries no version field at all and its description is frozen at v1.8.0
findings.correction: none on the file facts — .zenodo.json is 47 lines total, has no `version`, no `publication_date`, no `doi`; .zenodo.json:3 says "organised across six research pillars", narrates to "v1.8.0 delivers the first quantitative validation…", closes with "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" (vignettes/ holds 14 .Rmd); .Rbuildignore:11 is `^\.zenodo\.json$`; CITATION.cff:109-110 do carry version/date-released. SEVERITY DEFLATED because the stated impact is conditional on an unproven premise: nothing in the repo shows the GitHub→Zenodo integration is enabled, and RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:57-68 has the maintainer use Zenodo's manual "New version" web form, which never reads .zenodo.json. So the "immutable DOI record with no version label" scenario is possible but not demonstrated; what is demonstrated is two-major-versions-stale checked-in metadata.
findings.evidence: Half fixed. .zenodo.json now has both missing keys (version 0.9.0, publication_date 2026-07-27) and its description opens with ten research pillars, so the version half of the finding is closed by ac7b9c2 and a549528. The description half is not: the narrative still ends at v1.8.0 delivers the first quantitative validation of the Pillar 1 LLM extractor, so a deposit minted from this file would be labelled 0.9.0 while telling a v1.8.0 story, and its publication_date is two weeks behind HEAD.
findings.impact: If the GitHub-Zenodo integration is enabled and any tag is pushed, the resulting DOI record is published with NO version label and a description two major versions out of date (six pillars, v1.8.0, nine vignettes). That record is immutable. RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:63-65 tries to compensate by asking the maintainer to hand-type the version and description into the Zenodo web form, which means the checked-in metadata file is knowingly wrong and the correct metadata exists only as manual instructions.
findings.action: Add `"version": "3.10.0"` (or 3.11.0 per finding #1) and `"publication_date"` to .zenodo.json, and replace the .zenodo.json:3 description with the current 10-pillar text from DESCRIPTION:8-28 plus the v1.9.x-v3.10.0 highlights already written in cran-comments.md:105-132. Then the manual steps at RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:63-65 become unnecessary.

findings.title: The only DOI badge is a concept DOI the repo itself says resolves to v0.2.0, and nothing after v1.5.0 was ever deposited
findings.correction: File facts confirmed: README.md:7 is the sole DOI badge; RELEASE.md:17-18 (not :16-18) says the badge resolves to v0.2.0; the same concept DOI recurs at README.md:1728/:1737, cran-comments.md:103, inst/rosc/submission.md:22, INTRO.md:141, R/edaphos_zenodo_release.R:140/:202; RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71 still lists the deposit as pending; only 3 workflows exist. Two claims do not hold as stated: the badge row at README.md:4-13 holds 10 badges (plus 4 social badges at :15-18), not "nine badges at README.md:4-18"; and "nothing after v1.5.0 was ever deposited" is an inference from CITATION.cff, not something the repo states -- a v3.10.0 tag does exist and GitHub Releases cannot be checked offline.
findings.evidence: The core defect reproduces. README.md:7 is still the sole DOI badge and still the unannotated concept DOI: a zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.19683708.svg image linking to doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19683708. RELEASE.md:17 still states that the badge resolves to v0.2.0 and :135 still lists replacing it as an open action. Nothing after v1.5.0 has a deposit.
findings.impact: The badge row makes the package look archived and versioned when the newest archived artefact is v1.5.0/v1.6.0-era. A reader citing the badge DOI cites v0.2.0 content while reading 3.10.0 documentation. Combined with the version badge (README.md:9, 3.10.0), the release badge (likely rendering "no releases"), the tests badge (1345, unreproducible per finding #5) and the pillars badge (10/10, contradicted by the README's own six-pillar body per finding #10), four of the nine badges at README.md:4-18 misstate the project's state.
findings.action: Execute the Zenodo deposit (RELEASE-CHECKLIST-v3.10.0.md:51-71) so a version DOI exists, then add a version-DOI badge alongside the concept-DOI badge at README.md:7 and record the minted id in CITATION.cff. Add a release-publishing workflow so README.md:8 has Releases to report. Until the deposit exists, either remove RELEASE.md:16-18's known-stale badge or annotate it in the README as "concept DOI (all versions)" so readers do not mistake it for the current release.

findings.title: Two parallel version schemes collide inside a single README table: "v1.x roadmap lines" are interleaved with package 3.x versions, and v3.0.0 means two different things
findings.correction: none — README.md:1687-1717 verified verbatim, including the three v1.x rows placed below the v2.x block (:1714 v1.9.3 📝, :1715 v1.3.2 🚧, :1716 v1.8.3 📝) and :1717 `v3.0.0 | CRAN + rOpenSci submission | 📝`. NEWS.md:660 is `# edaphos 3.0.0` (shipped). NEWS.md:915 is `# edaphos 2.6.0` under the heading "Pilar 10 -- Graph Attention Networks", so README.md:1713's `v2.8.0 | Pilar 10` is the wrong version. `git log` confirms fd4ab0b (v1.8.3), 05cb516 (v1.9.3) and 7400a2c ("feat(v3.11.0): ... v1.3.2 ..."). NEWS has sections for 2.6.0/2.7.0/2.9.0/2.9.1/3.1.0-3.10.0, none of which appear as rows.
findings.evidence: The roadmap table is unchanged line for line. README.md:2147-2178 still interleaves the v1.x roadmap scheme with package 3.x versions and no marker separates them; the three v1.x rows still sit below the v2.x block, out of order and marked unfinished, at :2174-2176. The version reset makes it worse: the table's newest completed row is :2173 (v2.8.0) in a package whose DESCRIPTION:3 is 0.9.0.
findings.impact: A reader cannot tell whether "v1.3.2" is an older release than the current 3.10.0 (it looks like it) or an open work item (it is). The two schemes make the roadmap unreadable: three items shown as pending are done, one item shown as pending (v3.0.0 CRAN submission) shares its number with a release that shipped ten versions ago, and the pillar that defines the package's headline "10/10" badge is attributed to the wrong version. Anyone estimating project state from this table will be wrong in both directions simultaneously.
findings.action: Split the table in two: a "Released" table keyed strictly on DESCRIPTION versions (with every 2.6.0-3.10.0 row filled in, and Pilar 10 corrected from v2.8.0 to v2.6.0 at README.md:1713), and a separate "Open research promises" list that uses names rather than version numbers (e.g. "MoCo v2 200k-step re-benchmark", "CRAN + rOpenSci submission") so no roadmap item can ever collide with a release number again. Mark the three completed rows (README.md:1714-1716) as done and stop using v1.x strings in commit subjects for work landing in 3.x.

findings.title: Archival metadata (.zenodo.json, CITATION.cff) still describes a six-pillar package that stops at v1.8.0
findings.correction: none — .zenodo.json:3 verified (six-item `<ol>`, narrative ending at v1.8.0, "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" vs 14 .Rmd in vignettes/); CITATION.cff:7 "organised across six research pillars" and :33 "all six pillars"; RELEASE.md ~:53-55 does say "Copy the minted version DOI into `CITATION.cff` under `identifiers:` as a new entry, and also update `.zenodo.json` if it still points to an older DOI"; README's BibTeX at :1735 reads `version   = {2.8.0}` (the cited 1741-1752 range is ~6 lines low). This is the same defect as finding 3 with CITATION.cff added; severity is honest for stale citation metadata but it is not new information.
findings.evidence: `.zenodo.json:3` description enumerates six pillars in an `<ol>` and its narrative ends at "v1.8.0 delivers the first quantitative validation of the Pillar 1 LLM extractor" — no mention of pillars 7-10 (v2.3.0-v2.8.0), the v3.0.0 bridges, or anything in v3.1.0-v3.10.0. It also claims "nine mathematically-derived vignettes" while `vignettes/` holds 14 .Rmd files. `CITATION.cff:7` "organised across six research pillars" and :33 "integrates all six pillars". RELEASE.md:51-53 explicitly lists updating both as a post-Zenodo step ("Copy the minted version DOI into CITATION.cff ... and also update .zenodo.json if it still points to an older DOI") — never done. README.md:1741-1752 citation block still says `version = {2.8.0}`.
findings.impact: These two files are what Zenodo and citation tooling read. Publishing the v3.10.0 deposit (RELEASE-CHECKLIST step 3) would archive a description of a two-years-stale, six-pillar package under the current DOI, and `citation("edaphos")` / the README BibTeX would tell citing authors to reference v2.8.0.
